sources.authors: Khaled E. Ahmed, Jialing Song, Boqi Chen, Ou Wei, Bingzhou Zheng
sources.title: MCeT: Behavioral Model Correctness Evaluation using Large Language Models
sources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 28th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems (MODELS 2025), Grand Rapids, MI, USA, pp. 84-95
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (MODELS 2025 proceedings), IEEE Xplore (doc 11245361) and arXiv:2508.00630. Pages 84-95 and all five authors match exactly. First author's full name is Khaled E. Ahmed. Artefact repo: github.com/Huawei-TTE/MCeT.
sources.what_it_establishes: First fully automated LLM-based evaluation of a behavioural model (UML sequence diagrams) against free-text requirements, producing natural-language issue lists. Combines a holistic pass with a per-chunk/multi-perspective pass; detects 65% of human-reported issues (90% more than the holistic-only baseline) at 81% precision, and surfaces on average 6 issues per model that experienced engineers had missed.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ1 a hard quantitative baseline for the escalation problem: 35% of real issues are missed and ~19% of reported issues are false alarms. That residual is precisely the population a selective-intervention policy must route to a human, so MCeT's numbers are the 'do nothing / always trust the LLM' comparator the thesis must beat. Its holistic-vs-chunked agreement structure is also directly reusable as an uncertainty signal (disagreement between passes = candidate trigger for human judgment), and the 6 extra issues per model is evidence that the flow must be bidirectional (AI informs the expert, not only the reverse) - a claim the doctorate needs for the co-reasoning framing.

sources.authors: Syed Juned Ali, Iris Reinhartz-Berger, Dominik Bork
sources.title: How are LLMs Used for Conceptual Modeling? An Exploratory Study on Interaction Behavior and User Perception
sources.venue: Conceptual Modeling - 43rd International Conference (ER 2024), Pittsburgh, PA, USA, Oct 28-31 2024, LNCS, Springer, pp. 257-275
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp and SpringerLink (chapter DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-75872-0_14, in the ER 2024 proceedings volume 10.1007/978-3-031-75872-0). Authors, year, pages 257-275 all match. A companion dataset ('Manually Annotated Event Log of User Prompts in LLMs for Conceptual Modeling') exists at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13513891.
sources.what_it_establishes: Empirical study of 76 undergraduate IS students in 39 groups doing UML use case and class (domain) modelling with LLM assistance. Characterises actual interaction behaviour (prompting patterns, iteration, acceptance) and relates it to perceived usefulness, showing that the open-endedness of the LLM interface produces highly divergent interaction behaviours that condition perceived value.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the closest existing instrument for SQ1's measurement problem - it operationalises 'how does a human actually engage an AI modelling assistant, and when' with an annotated prompt event log. The doctorate can reuse that coding scheme to define expert-burden metrics (interactions per model, time-to-judgment) and to distinguish voluntary intervention from system-requested intervention. It is also methodologically load-bearing because it is co-authored by the doctoral supervisor (Reinhartz-Berger) in the same student-produced-domain-model setting as VEGO-AI, so the study population and artefact type are directly comparable and its protocol can be defended as prior practice in the group.

sources.authors: Sofia Ananieva, Sandra Greiner, Timo Kehrer, Jacob Krüger, Thomas Kühn, Lukas Linsbauer, Sten Grüner, Anne Koziolek, Henrik Lönn, S. Ramesh, Ralf Reussner
sources.title: A conceptual model for unifying variability in space and time: Rationale, validation, and illustrative applications
sources.venue: Empirical Software Engineering, 27(5), article 101
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (journals/ese/AnanievaGKKKLGK22), SpringerLink and TU/e repository. Volume 27, issue 5, article 101, 2022 all match. Note the VEGO-AI reference list truncates the subtitle - the full published title includes ': Rationale, validation, and illustrative applications'. The VEGO-AI entry cites 'Ananieva, S. et al.' - the full author list is 11 people as given here.
sources.what_it_establishes: A validated, unified conceptual model and terminology for variability in space (concurrent variants) and time (evolution), consolidating fragmented SPL vocabularies so that researchers and tools can compare and interoperate. Includes an explicit rationale, an expert validation of the conceptual model, and illustrative applications to real tooling.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: SQ2 requires a representation for expert judgment that is stable enough to be stored, reconciled and reused - and this paper is the discipline's reference example of building exactly such a representation for variability itself, plus a defensible method for validating a conceptual model with domain experts rather than asserting it. The doctorate can lift both the schema design pattern (unify competing vocabularies into one conceptual model, then validate) and the space/time distinction: judgments about variability decay over time as guidelines evolve, so 'variability in time' is the vocabulary for reasoning about when a stored judgment becomes stale and must not be generalised. It is the strongest available precedent for the thesis's own judgment-representation contribution.

sources.authors: Ludovic Auxepaules, Dominique Py, Thierry Lemeunier
sources.title: A Diagnosis Method that Matches Class Diagrams in a Learning Environment for Object-Oriented Modeling
sources.venue: 8th IEEE International Conference on Advanced Learning Technologies (ICALT 2008), Santander, Spain, pp. 26-30
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp, HAL (hal-01452789) and Semantic Scholar. Authors, year, venue and pages 26-30 match. dblp gives DOI 10.1109/ICALT.2008.187; note the VEGO-AI-adjacent sources sometimes show .184 - use the dblp value and re-check against IEEE Xplore before final submission.
sources.what_it_establishes: A graph-matching diagnosis algorithm inside the Diagram learning environment that compares a student's UML class diagram against an expert reference diagram, schematising both into characteristic structural patterns to identify differences and drive pedagogical feedback.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the cleanest statement of the assumption the whole doctorate attacks: that a difference from the reference solution is an error. Its structural pattern matching can detect that two diagrams differ but has no concept at all of a difference being a legitimate alternative - which is exactly the substantial-vs-occasional distinction VEGO-AI introduces. For the thesis it is the historical anchor of the gap narrative in Chapter 2/3, and a useful contrast case for SQ2: purely structural difference detection produces no reusable knowledge, because it stores no rationale for why a difference was acceptable.

sources.authors: Weiyi Bian, Omar Alam, Jörg Kienzle
sources.title: Automated Grading of Class Diagrams
sources.venue: 2019 ACM/IEEE 22nd International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems Companion (MODELS-C 2019), Munich, Germany, pp. 700-709
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (MoDELS Companion 2019) and IEEE. Authors, year, pages 700-709 and DOI 10.1109/MODELS-C.2019.00106 all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: An automated grading approach for UML class diagrams that maps student model elements onto an instructor's reference solution using syntactic and semantic similarity, then assigns marks from a rubric - motivated by consistency, fairness and scale in large classes.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The canonical single-correct-solution grading baseline that VEGO-AI and this doctorate displace. Its value to the thesis is defining the failure mode precisely: a rubric plus a reference mapping encodes the instructor's judgment once, opaquely and non-negotiably, with no mechanism for the instructor to revise it, no record of why an alternative was rejected, and no way to reuse the decision in another course. That is a compact statement of the SQ2 problem (judgment stored as parameters rather than as governed, inspectable, revisable knowledge), so it is the right foil when the thesis argues for an explicit judgment store over rubric tuning.

sources.authors: Weiyi Bian, Omar Alam, Jörg Kienzle
sources.title: Is automated grading of models effective? Assessing automated grading of class diagrams
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd ACM/IEEE International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems (MODELS 2020), pp. 365-376
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp, the MODELS 2020 technical-track programme page (conf.researchr.org) and ACM DL. Authors, year and pages 365-376 match. DOI is the ACM one, 10.1145/3365438.3410944.
sources.what_it_establishes: Empirical evaluation of automated model grading in two real courses - a beginner class of 103 students producing an object-oriented design model and an advanced class of 89 students producing a domain model - assessing where automated grades agree with and diverge from human instructors.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The direct empirical predecessor for SQ1's core question of where automation is not trustworthy enough to act alone. Its human-vs-automated divergence analysis is the evidence base for defining the escalation set, and its two-cohort design (beginner vs advanced, design model vs domain model) is a ready-made template for the thesis's own evaluation: it shows that agreement is not a single number but varies by cohort and artefact type, which is exactly the transfer sensitivity SQ3 must characterise. Also gives the thesis a defensible sample-size and setting precedent when justifying its own study design to the committee.

sources.authors: Nacir Bouali, Marcus Gerhold, Tosif Ul Rehman, Faizan Ahmed
sources.title: Toward Automated UML Diagram Assessment: Comparing LLM-Generated Scores with Teaching Assistants
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Computer Supported Education (CSEDU 2025), Volume 1, Porto, Portugal, April 1-3 2025, SciTePress, pp. 158-169
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SciTePress (paper 134819), researchr CSEDU 2025 Vol. 1 proceedings listing and the University of Twente research portal. Authors, year, pages 158-169 and DOI 10.5220/0013481900003932 match. Third author's full name is Tosif Ul Rehman.
sources.what_it_establishes: Compares grades from three teaching assistants against three LLMs (Llama, GPT o1-mini, Claude) on 92 real student UML class diagram submissions, after converting diagrams to textual descriptions. GPT o1-mini and Claude Sonnet reach correlation above 0.76 with human graders and mean absolute error below 4.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most current human-vs-LLM agreement baseline in exactly the doctorate's artefact type and population, so it is the number an SQ1 selective-intervention policy has to improve on - and improving a 0.76 correlation is only worth doing on the subset where the models are actually unreliable, which is the thesis's whole argument. More importantly for SQ2, the three-TA design exposes inter-human disagreement: if the TAs disagree among themselves, there is no single ground-truth judgment to store, and the thesis must handle reconciliation of conflicting expert judgments rather than assume one authoritative expert. This paper supplies the empirical hook for that argument.

sources.authors: Maxim Bragilovski, A. T. van Can, Fabiano Dalpiaz, Arnon Sturm
sources.title: Leveraging machines to derive domain models from user stories
sources.venue: Requirements Engineering, 30(2), pp. 241-262, Springer
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, Utrecht University research portal and ACM DL. Volume 30, issue 2, pages 241-262, 2025 and DOI 10.1007/s00766-025-00442-9 all match. Replication package at Zenodo record 15223349. I did not independently confirm the second author's full given names beyond the initials 'A. T.' as cited.
sources.what_it_establishes: An end-to-end machine-learning pipeline, built via deliberate feature engineering, that derives both classes and associations for a domain model from a collection of user stories - with an open replication package of code, results and datasets.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Written by two of the VEGO-AI authors (Bragilovski and Sturm, with Dalpiaz), this is the upstream automation the governed-judgment layer sits on top of: it produces candidate domain models, and the doctorate governs what happens when those candidates differ from each other or from an expert's expectation. Practically it hands the thesis a shared task definition, an open dataset and a replication package for domain-model derivation, which lowers the cost of building an SQ3 transfer study across a second guideline-operationalisation context (user-story-derived models vs student-produced models) without constructing a new corpus from scratch.

sources.authors: Marco Calamo, Massimo Mecella, Monique Snoeck
sources.title: Assessing the Suitability of Large Language Models in Generating UML Class Diagrams as Conceptual Models
sources.venue: Enterprise, Business-Process and Information Systems Modeling - BPMDS 2025 / EMMSAD 2025, Vienna, Austria, June 16-17 2025, LNBIP vol. 558, Springer, pp. 211-226
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (BPMDS 2025) and SpringerLink. Authors, year, pages 211-226, LNBIP volume 558 and DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-95397-2_13 all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: An assessment of whether LLM-generated UML class diagrams are fit to serve as conceptual models - i.e. judged not just as syntactically valid diagrams but against conceptual-modelling quality expectations - identifying where LLM output falls short of that standard.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the quality-criteria vocabulary the doctorate needs to say what a human is being asked to judge. SQ1 cannot define an escalation trigger without a notion of which deficiencies matter, and this paper separates 'syntactically fine' from 'conceptually adequate' in the thesis's exact artefact type. Snoeck's conceptual-modelling quality lineage (KU Leuven, MERODE) makes this a citable authority for the quality dimensions along which substantial variability is assessed, rather than the thesis inventing its own criteria.

sources.authors: Javier Cámara, Javier Troya, Lola Burgueño, Antonio Vallecillo
sources.title: On the assessment of generative AI in modeling tasks: an experience report with ChatGPT and UML
sources.venue: Software and Systems Modeling (SoSyM), 22(3), pp. 781-793, Springer
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, ACM DL and the University of Malaga repository. Volume 22, pages 781-793, 2023 and DOI 10.1007/s10270-023-01105-5 match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Widely-cited experience report showing that, unlike code generation, ChatGPT's performance on software modelling tasks is limited: syntactic and semantic deficiencies, lack of consistency across responses to the same prompt, and scalability problems.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The 'lack of consistency in responses' finding is the single most important citation for SQ2's governance requirement. If the same model answers the same modelling question differently on repeated runs, then a judgment captured from one run cannot be safely generalised to a class of cases - which is precisely why reuse must be validated and reconciled rather than cached. The thesis can cite this to argue that non-determinism, not just error rate, is what makes an ungoverned judgment store unsafe, and to justify storing provenance (model, prompt, run) alongside every retained judgment. It is also the standard reference for the reliability gap that motivates keeping human authority in the loop.

sources.authors: Meriem Ben Chaaben, Lola Burgueño, Istvan David, Houari Sahraoui
sources.title: On the Utility of Domain Modeling Assistance with Large Language Models
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.12577 (submitted 16 Oct 2024); subsequently published in ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
sources.verification_note: arXiv:2410.12577 confirmed with matching title, all four authors and the Oct 2024 submission date; affiliations confirmed as Universite de Montreal (Ben Chaaben, Sahraoui), University of Malaga (Burgueno), McMaster University (David). IMPORTANT UPDATE: a journal version now exists in ACM TOSEM (DOI 10.1145/3744920) - I could not open the ACM record directly (403) but the ACM listing surfaced consistently in search. Consider citing the TOSEM version rather than the preprint.
sources.what_it_establishes: A study of the actual usefulness of LLM-plus-few-shot-prompting assistance for domain modelling, deliberately avoiding the need for large domain-specific training corpora, and evaluating whether modellers benefit from the generated suggestions across several modelling activities.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the closest existing treatment of SQ1's cost side. Where most related work asks 'is the AI accurate', this one asks 'is the assistance actually useful to the human', which is the utility-versus-burden trade-off the selective-intervention policy has to optimise. Its evaluation design gives the thesis a way to measure the cost of a wrongly-triggered request for human judgment (wasted expert attention, ignored suggestions), not just the cost of a missed one - and a defensible answer to the obvious committee challenge that more human involvement is trivially better. The few-shot framing also matters for SQ2: few-shot exemplars are a primitive, ungoverned form of judgment reuse, and the thesis can position its judgment store as the governed alternative.

sources.authors: Kua Chen, Boqi Chen, Yujing Yang, Gunter Mussbacher, Dániel Varró
sources.title: Embedding-based Automated Assessment of Domain Models
sources.venue: MODELS Companion '24 - Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 27th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems: Companion Proceedings (Educators Symposium), pp. 87-94
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL and the MODELS 2024 Educators Symposium programme page. Authors, year, pages 87-94 and DOI 10.1145/3652620.3687774 match; published 31 Oct 2024.
sources.what_it_establishes: Uses embedding-based semantic similarity to compare student-generated domain models against a reference solution for automated assessment at scale, addressing the manual-grading bottleneck as software engineering enrolments grow.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Provides a concrete retrieval mechanism for SQ2's reuse problem. Reusing stored expert judgment requires deciding when a new model element is 'the same case' as one already judged, and embedding similarity over model elements is the obvious candidate - this paper shows it working on precisely this artefact type and gives the thesis a citable baseline for the matching component rather than an ad hoc string comparison. It also marks the boundary the doctorate must not cross: similarity alone licenses retrieval, not automatic application of the prior judgment, which is exactly the unsafe-generalisation line SQ2 and SQ3 are about.

sources.authors: Kua Chen, Yujing Yang, Boqi Chen, José Antonio Hernández López, Gunter Mussbacher, Dániel Varró
sources.title: Automated Domain Modeling with Large Language Models: A Comparative Study
sources.venue: 2023 ACM/IEEE 26th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems (MODELS 2023), pp. 162-172
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp, the MODELS 2023 technical-track programme page and the Universidad de Murcia repository. Authors, year, pages 162-172 and DOI 10.1109/MODELS58315.2023.00037 match. Artefacts at Zenodo record 8116032. Author affiliations: McGill University, Universidad de Murcia, Linkoping University.
sources.what_it_establishes: Systematic comparative evaluation of multiple LLMs on automated domain modelling, establishing the capability envelope and the evaluation metrics (element-level precision/recall against reference models) that the subfield has largely adopted since.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The metric convention this paper set is what the doctorate's evaluation will be read against, so adopting or explicitly departing from it is a defensibility decision, not a detail. Substantively it is the strongest evidence that LLM performance on domain modelling varies by model and configuration, which means a judgment captured under one configuration may not hold under another - a direct input to SQ2's provenance and validation requirements, and to SQ3's transfer question. It also gives the thesis its 'automation-only' comparator: the delta between this and VEGO-AI-plus-governed-judgment is the doctorate's headline claim.

sources.authors: Hoa Khanh Dam
sources.title: Towards Multi-Agentic AI for automated software design and modelling: challenges and opportunities
sources.venue: 2025 40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering Workshops (ASEW 2025), MAS-GAIN workshop, Seoul, South Korea, pp. 311-314
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp, the ASE 2025 / MAS-GAIN 2025 programme page and the IEEE Computer Society digital library ASEW 2025 table of contents. Single author, pages 311-314, DOI 10.1109/ASEW67777.2025.00063. Note the VEGO-AI reference list truncates the subtitle - the full title includes ': challenges and opportunities'. Author is Prof. Hoa Khanh Dam, University of Wollongong.
sources.what_it_establishes: A vision/position paper proposing a conceptual multi-agentic AI framework of autonomous goal-driven agents for software design, and naming the open challenges explicitly: translating natural-language requirements into design models, resolving ambiguities, maintaining consistency within and between design models, and managing conflicts and inconsistencies when merging different versions of a design model.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most direct citable statement of the SQ2 gap available. Dam names conflict and inconsistency management across agent-produced model versions as an open challenge and stops there - proposing no governance mechanism, no human authority model, and no account of how a resolution is retained for reuse. That is the hole the doctorate fills, and because it is a 2025 vision paper from a senior figure at an ASE workshop it is exactly the kind of reference a committee accepts as independent evidence that the problem is live and unsolved, rather than one the candidate invented. It also legitimises the multi-agent framing that VEGO-AI's four-agent architecture already commits to.

sources.authors: Sascha El-Sharkawy, Nozomi Yamagishi-Eichler, Klaus Schmid
sources.title: Metrics for analyzing variability and its implementation in software product lines: A systematic literature review
sources.venue: Information and Software Technology, vol. 106, pp. 1-30, Elsevier
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp, ScienceDirect (article S0950584918301873) and the University of Hildesheim SSE publication list. Volume 106, pages 1-30, 2019 and DOI 10.1016/j.infsof.2018.08.015 match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Systematic literature review cataloguing metrics for variability and its implementation in software product lines, establishing that conventional software-engineering metrics do not transfer to SPLs because they ignore variability management, and organising the alternatives that do.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Two distinct uses. First, its catalogue is the candidate feature set for quantifying variability - the measurable properties (spread, frequency, dispersion across variants) that could operationalise 'systematic' versus 'sporadic' in the substantial/occasional distinction, giving SQ1's escalation trigger a quantitative basis rather than leaving it purely to LLM judgment. Second, its central finding is a transfer failure - metrics valid in one context become invalid when variability enters - which is the structural analogue of SQ3's unsafe-generalisation risk and lets the thesis argue that context-blind reuse of measures is a known, documented failure in this field, not a hypothetical. It is also a methodological precedent if the doctorate runs its own SLR.

sources.authors: Alessio Ferrari, Sallam Abualhaija, Chetan Arora
sources.title: Model Generation with LLMs: From Requirements to UML Sequence Diagrams
sources.venue: 2024 IEEE 32nd International Requirements Engineering Conference Workshops (REW 2024), pp. 291-300
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (RE Workshops 2024), Semantic Scholar and arXiv:2404.06371. Authors, year, pages 291-300 and DOI 10.1109/REW61692.2024.00044 match. An open preprint is available at arXiv:2404.06371 (v2).
sources.what_it_establishes: Qualitative study of ChatGPT-generated UML sequence diagrams for 28 requirements documents spanning different types and domains. Generated models generally conform to the notation and are reasonably understandable, but completeness and correctness are affected.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The 28-documents-across-domains design is the cross-context evidence SQ3 needs: it shows that LLM modelling reliability is not a single constant but shifts with document type and domain, which is the precise mechanism by which a judgment validated in one guideline-operationalisation context becomes unsafe in another. Its conform-but-incomplete result also refines what the human is for - the escalation trigger cannot be notational validity, since that is the part the LLM reliably gets right, and must instead target completeness and semantic correctness. Finally, by moving from class diagrams to behavioural models it lets the thesis argue transfer across artefact types within software/modelling before ever approaching the healthcare context in SQ3.

sources.authors: Matthias Galster, Danny Weyns, Dan Tofan, Bartosz Michalik, Paris Avgeriou
sources.title: Variability in Software Systems - A Systematic Literature Review
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 40(3), 282-306
sources.verification_note: Paper, authors, title, volume/issue and page range all confirmed via Crossref/IEEE and the author's open PDF (cs.rug.nl/~paris/papers/TSE14.pdf). The ONLY divergence is the year: the VEGO-AI reference says 2013, but the journal issue is Vol. 40, No. 3, March 2014. The '2013' comes from the DOI string (10.1109/TSE.2013.56, IEEE's online-first year). Recommend citing as 2014.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical SLR on variability in software systems: 15,430 papers screened across 13 journals and 18 conferences, 196 analysed. Maps how variability is handled across requirements, architecture, design, implementation and testing, and shows the field treats variability almost exclusively as *intentional, planned* variation (configuration options, features, product-line variation points).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives the thesis its baseline definition of 'variability' and, crucially, the GAP that VEGO-AI's substantial/occasional distinction fills: the SLR shows the literature assumes variability is designed-in and legitimate by construction, so it has no vocabulary for variability that is *sporadic or erroneous*. Use it in the background chapter to justify why 'not all differences matter' is a genuinely new problem framing, and to argue that because pre-LLM variability research never had to separate meaningful from accidental difference, it also never needed a mechanism for human judgment - which is exactly what SQ1/SQ2 introduce.
sources.citation_use: Background/foundation - definitional anchor for variability and evidence that classical variability research presumes intentional variation, hence no need for judgment governance.

sources.authors: Markus Hamann, Sebastian Götz, Uwe Aßmann
sources.title: Towards an Interoperable Model-driven Automated Assessment System for Computer Science Education
sources.venue: MODELS Companion '24 (ACM/IEEE 27th Int. Conf. on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems: Companion Proceedings), 95-102
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL and dblp: MoDELS (Companion) 2024, pp. 95-102, DOI 10.1145/3652620.3687775. Third author is spelled 'Aßmann' (Assmann) at TU Dresden - the VEGO-AI reference's 'Assmann, U.' is the correct transliteration.
sources.what_it_establishes: Argues that the automated-assessment landscape in CS education is fragmented into siloed, non-interoperable systems, and proposes a model-driven architecture with common exchange representations so assessment logic and artefacts can move between systems. Motivated by the fact that student numbers rose while educator feedback time did not.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Direct methodological input for SQ2. SQ2 asks how expert judgment should be *represented and stored* so it can be reused; this paper is the closest existing attempt at a portable, model-driven representation layer for assessment - but it standardises the *task and grading artefacts*, not the *judgment rationale*. That asymmetry is the thesis's opening: the doctorate can adopt their interoperability argument wholesale and then show that an interoperable schema for judgments (with provenance, scope-of-validity, and authority markers) does not yet exist. Also supplies the workload/scalability motivation for SQ1's 'without unnecessary expert burden' clause.
sources.citation_use: RQ2 - prior art on representation/interoperability of assessment artefacts; contrast case showing artefact schemas exist but judgment schemas do not.

sources.authors: María Blanca Ibáñez, María Lucía Barrón-Estrada, Ramón Zatarain-Cabada
sources.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Grade Like an Expert? A Study on UML Class Diagram Assessment Accuracy
sources.venue: Computer Applications in Engineering Education 33(5), article e70080
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on Wiley Online Library: Vol. 33, Issue 5, 2025, article e70080, DOI 10.1002/cae.70080. Note the article is identified by an e-locator (e70080), not a classical page range.
sources.what_it_establishes: Empirical head-to-head: 34 engineering students' UML class diagrams (a SOLID-principles design task) graded independently by three expert instructors and four multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Amazon AI, Claude 3.5 Sonnet). Finding: MLLMs show promising partial-score alignment with experts but consistent, significant failures in semantic interpretation and evaluative reasoning, producing inconsistencies.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the strongest published *evidence base* for SQ1's premise. SQ1 only makes sense if there exists an identifiable class of cases where the model's judgment is unreliable and a human's is not; this paper localises that class empirically - shallow/structural checks align with experts, semantic and evaluative-reasoning judgments do not. The thesis can lift that as the operational definition of 'important uncertainty' that should trigger escalation, and use the same task setting (student UML diagrams) as a near-identical evaluation context to VEGO-AI. It is also the honest counterweight to any claim that LLM grading is solved.
sources.citation_use: RQ1 - empirical justification for selective escalation; supplies the failure taxonomy (semantic vs structural) that an escalation trigger can be built on.

sources.authors: Haolin Jin, Linghan Huang, Haipeng Cai, Jun Yan, Bo Li, Huaming Chen
sources.title: From LLMs to LLM-based Agents for Software Engineering: A Survey of Current, Challenges and Future
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2408.02479 (v1 5 Aug 2024; v2 13 Apr 2025)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on arXiv and NASA ADS (2024arXiv240802479J). Full title includes the subtitle 'A Survey of Current, Challenges and Future', which the VEGO-AI reference abbreviates. Preprint - no peer-reviewed venue found.
sources.what_it_establishes: Survey of LLMs and LLM-based agents across six SE topics: requirements engineering, code generation, autonomous decision-making, software design, test generation, software maintenance. Frames agents as LLMs used as a decision-making and action-taking core, addressing LLM limits in autonomy and self-improvement.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Positioning and gap-mapping rather than mechanism. Its taxonomy lets the thesis place VEGO-AI's four-agent architecture inside the agentic-SE landscape and, more usefully, show what the taxonomy *omits*: the survey's dimensions are autonomy, planning, tool use and self-improvement - human authority, escalation policy and judgment persistence are not first-class categories. Cite it to evidence that 'more autonomy' is the field's default trajectory, then argue the doctorate's umbrella question (governed human judgment) is orthogonal to and corrective of that trajectory. Weak as a primary source (preprint, broad survey); strong as a landscape citation.
sources.citation_use: Foundation/positioning - agentic-SE landscape map and evidence that human governance is absent from the field's organising taxonomy.

sources.authors: Nataliia Klievtsova, Janik-Vasily Benzin, Timotheus Kampik, Juergen Mangler, Stefanie Rinderle-Ma
sources.title: Conversational Process Modelling: State of the Art, Applications, and Implications in Practice
sources.venue: Business Process Management Forum (BPM 2023 Forum), LNBIP vol. 490, Springer, 319-336
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink and the TUM research portal: LNBIP 490, pp. 319-336, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-41623-1_19. All five authors, venue and page range match exactly.
sources.what_it_establishes: Systematic analysis of existing chatbots for conversational process modelling, evaluated on real higher-education process datasets, with application scenarios positioned along the process life cycle plus practical guidance and open research needs.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the *interaction-design* half of SQ1. SQ1 asks not only when to request human judgment but *how*; this paper is the closest systematic treatment of dialogue as the elicitation channel between a modelling system and a domain expert, and it does it life-cycle-phase by life-cycle-phase - a structure the thesis can reuse to decide at which VEGO-AI stage an escalation dialogue belongs. The limitation the thesis exploits: conversation here is user-initiated and open-ended (the human drives), whereas SQ1 needs the *system* to decide when to interrupt. That inversion is a clean contribution statement.
sources.citation_use: RQ1 - prior art on human-system dialogue in modelling; contrast that establishes user-initiated vs system-initiated escalation as the delta.

sources.authors: Andreas Metzger, Klaus Pohl
sources.title: Software product line engineering and variability management: achievements and challenges
sources.venue: FOSE 2014 (Future of Software Engineering Proceedings, at ICSE '14, Hyderabad), ACM, 70-84
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL and the University of Duisburg-Essen bibliography: FOSE 2014, pp. 70-84, DOI 10.1145/2593882.2593888. An open preprint is hosted at sse.uni-due.de.
sources.what_it_establishes: Authoritative roadmap paper summarising SPLE research achievements against a standard product-line framework, identifying variability modelling and (informally) verified product-line artefacts as the strongest results, and naming the open challenges and intersections (services, cloud, big data, autonomic and adaptive systems).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: A gap-legitimation source. Written by the field's agenda-setters, it enumerates what variability management had and had not solved - and human judgment governance appears nowhere on that agenda. Cite it to show the omission is structural, not an oversight of one paper. Its 'achievements vs challenges' framing is also a usable template for the thesis's own state-of-the-art chapter, and its emphasis on *verified* artefacts connects to SQ2's 'validated, reconciled' requirement: SPLE verified artefacts formally; SQ2 must validate judgments socially/epistemically instead.
sources.citation_use: Foundation - agenda-level evidence that variability management never scoped human judgment as a managed asset.

sources.authors: Klaus Pohl, Günter Böckle, Frank J. van der Linden
sources.title: Software Product Line Engineering: Foundations, Principles and Techniques
sources.venue: Springer, Berlin/Heidelberg (book)
sources.verification_note: Verified via Crossref (DOI 10.1007/3-540-28901-1 resolves to title 'Software Product Line Engineering', Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2005, authors Pohl/Böckle/van der Linden) and ISBN 978-3-540-24372-4. Minor: the printed subtitle is 'Foundations, Principles and Techniques' (no comma before 'and'); the VEGO-AI reference adds a serial comma.
sources.what_it_establishes: The standard textbook defining the SPLE framework: the split between domain engineering and application engineering, the variability model, and variation points/variants as first-class artefacts.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Terminological bedrock - the thesis needs a single citable definition of variation point, variant and binding to keep 'variability' from drifting between the SPLE sense and VEGO-AI's sense. It also supplies the conceptual move SQ2 imitates: SPLE's core insight is that reusable knowledge must be *separated into a domain-engineering asset base* before it can be applied per-product. SQ2 proposes the same two-level structure for judgment (a governed judgment base vs its per-case application), which lets the thesis frame governed knowledge reuse as an SPLE-shaped idea applied to human reasoning rather than to code.
sources.citation_use: Foundation - definitional source for variability terminology and the domain/application two-level reuse structure SQ2 mirrors.

sources.authors: Matias Pol'la, Agustina Buccella, Alejandra Cechich
sources.title: Analysis of variability models: a systematic literature review
sources.venue: Software and Systems Modeling (SoSyM) 20, 1043-1077
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink: SoSyM vol. 20, pp. 1043-1077, 2021, DOI 10.1007/s10270-020-00839-w (online first Dec 2020). Authors, year, volume and pages all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: SLR classifying variability *models* and the analysis operations performed on them, covering how variability management lets engineers derive a family of applications from a manageable range of variable functionality according to expert users' needs.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most recent systematic account of what a variability model *is* and what can be computed over it - the yardstick against which the thesis must show that VEGO-AI-style variability in student domain models is not analysable by existing formalisms. Two specific uses: (a) it demonstrates that variability analysis is treated as a decidable computation over a formal model, whereas substantial-vs-occasional is a judgment call, motivating the human-in-the-loop turn; (b) its 'expert users' needs' framing shows expert input enters SPLE only at model-construction time and is never revisited, validated or reconciled afterwards - precisely the lifecycle gap SQ2 targets.
sources.citation_use: Foundation - state of the art in variability model analysis; evidence that variability analysis is formal/decidable while VEGO-AI's distinction is judgmental.

sources.authors: Asha Rajbhoj, Akanksha Somase, Tanay Sant, Sushant Vale, Vinay Kulkarni
sources.title: LLM4Model: Automated Requirements Specification Model Authoring
sources.venue: CAiSE 2025 Forum (Intelligent Information Systems: CAiSE 2025 Forum and Doctoral Consortium, Vienna, 16-20 June 2025), Springer, 128-136
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, dblp and the CAiSE 2025 programme site: pp. 128-136, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-94590-8_16, session 'AI and Large Language Models for Process and Knowledge Engineering', 20 June 2025. Important nuance: this is the CAiSE **Forum** (short/tool track), not the CAiSE main research track - worth stating if the thesis weighs evidence strength.
sources.what_it_establishes: A configurable, extensible, domain-agnostic tool that uses LLMs to author machine-processable requirements specification models from text, aimed at reducing the cognitive load of an intellect-intensive manual task; demonstrated on two industrial case studies.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Useful mainly as an industrial-practice data point and as a design contrast. Its 'configurable and extensible' architecture is the kind of substrate SQ2's judgment store would have to plug into, and its two real-world case studies give the thesis evidence that LLM-driven model authoring is already leaving the lab. The contrast: LLM4Model optimises for *removing* human effort (cognitive-load reduction) with no account of when the human must stay in the loop or how their corrections are retained - the exact opposite of SQ1's 'selective' framing, where some human effort is deliberately preserved because it is load-bearing. Cite it as the efficiency-maximising pole against which governed judgment is positioned.
sources.citation_use: General/related work - industrial LLM model-authoring tool; efficiency-first design contrasted with selective-intervention design.

sources.authors: Marcello La Rosa, Wil M. P. van der Aalst, Marlon Dumas, Fredrik P. Milani
sources.title: Business Process Variability Modeling: A Survey
sources.venue: ACM Computing Surveys 50(1), 1-45
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL: ACM Computing Surveys Vol. 50, No. 1, March 2017, DOI 10.1145/3041957, 45 pages. Note the first author's surname is 'La Rosa' - the VEGO-AI reference renders it 'Rosa, M. L.', which will sort and format incorrectly in most bibliography styles and should be fixed.
sources.what_it_establishes: Systematic inventory and comparative evaluation of customisable process modelling approaches, with criteria for selecting among them and an explicit statement of gaps in the state of the art; motivated by organisations maintaining families of process variants that conventional BPM languages cannot express.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The cross-domain evidence that the variability problem is not confined to software - it recurs wherever a family of similar artefacts must be maintained. That matters directly for SQ3: the thesis claims judgment can transfer across guideline-operationalisation contexts, and this survey supplies the second, independent domain (business processes) plus the vocabulary for comparing variability constructs across formalisms. It is also the closest analogue to healthcare guideline variation - clinical pathways are process variants - so it is the safest published bridge toward the healthcare ambition in SQ3 without prematurely citing clinical literature.
sources.citation_use: Foundation/RQ3 bridge - cross-domain evidence for variability families and the comparison framework for transfer across formalisms.

sources.authors: Malik Abdul Sami, Muhammad Waseem, Zeeshan Rasheed, Mika Saari, Kari Systä, Pekka Abrahamsson
sources.title: Experimenting with Multi-Agent Software Development: Towards a Unified Platform
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.05381 (submitted 8 June 2024)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on arXiv (2406.05381), all six authors and title match exactly. Preprint - no peer-reviewed venue located; the same group's related work appears at PROFES 2024, but this specific paper appears to remain a preprint.
sources.what_it_establishes: An experimental multi-agent platform assigning LLM agents to distinct SDLC roles (requirements, design, code, test) to work toward end-to-end automated software development, reporting on the integration challenges of unifying them.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Architectural comparator for the VEGO-AI four-agent design, and a cautionary source. Its value to the thesis is negative evidence: role-specialised multi-agent SE platforms hand off between agents but have no defined point at which a human enters, no representation of a human decision, and no record of who authorised what - so failures propagate through the chain. That is the concrete failure mode SQ1 and SQ2 are designed to prevent, and it lets the thesis argue for governance from an observed weakness rather than from principle alone. Treat as preprint-grade evidence; do not lean on its empirical claims.
sources.citation_use: General/related work - multi-agent SE architecture comparator and illustration of ungoverned agent-to-agent handoff.

sources.authors: Jonathan Silva Mercado, Qin Ma, Jordi Cabot, Pierre Kelsen, Henderik A. Proper
sources.title: Towards Human-in-the-Loop LLM-Enabled Domain Modeling
sources.venue: Conceptual Modeling - ER 2025 (44th Int. Conf. on Conceptual Modeling, Poitiers, France, 20-23 Oct 2025), LNCS vol. 16189, Springer, 127-145
sources.verification_note: Existence, DOI, page range and venue CONFIRMED: SpringerLink DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-08623-5_7, LNCS 16189 (eds. Bork, Lukyanenko, Sadiq, Bellatreche, Pastor), pp. 127-145; the ER 2025 official programme (er2025.ensma.fr) lists it in main-track session 'ER Papers 3: LLM-enabled Modeling', Tue 21 Oct, 14:30-15:00, room A101. TWO metadata divergences from the VEGO-AI reference: (1) the first author's full surname is 'Silva Mercado', not 'Silva' - citing as 'Silva, J.' may misattribute; (2) Springer's citation year is 2026 (proceedings imprint), while the conference was 2025. Cite as ER 2025 but expect Springer/Google Scholar to render 2026. I could not retrieve the full text (paywalled); the method description below comes from the publisher abstract and the ER programme, not from reading the paper.
sources.what_it_establishes: An LLM-based domain-modelling method with a human in the loop. An LLM produces an initial draft domain model from a textual domain description; the draft then enters a feedback loop moderated by a RULE-BASED AGENT that engages the user in a Q&A dialogue. The rule-based agent selects which questions to ask based on their potential to clarify the MOST UNCERTAIN aspects of the model so far. Explicit motivation: raw LLM output is degraded by hallucination and inconsistency, so automatic creation is combined with human supervision.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: THE closest published work to SQ1 - treat it as a partial answer and a competitor for the RQ1 novelty claim, not as background. Read precisely: (A) It is a FOUNDATION for the mechanism. It establishes the exact architectural pattern SQ1 needs - a separate, non-LLM arbiter that decides what to ask the human, with question selection ranked by expected uncertainty reduction. The thesis should adopt this as prior art and build on it rather than reinvent it; the rule-based moderator is also a governance asset, because a rule-based selector is auditable in a way an LLM selector is not. (B) It is a COMPETITOR on part of SQ1. SQ1's first half - 'when should the system request human judgment' - is substantially addressed here via uncertainty-ranked question selection, so the doctorate can no longer claim that question is open. The honest positioning is that Silva Mercado et al. answer 'when' for a single-model, single-session drafting task. (C) The DELTAS the thesis must own, which are real and defensible: (1) SCOPE OF THE JUDGMENT - their uncertainty is about model *content* (is this a class? is this relation right?) in a greenfield drafting task; VEGO-AI's uncertainty is second-order, about whether a *difference between models* is substantial or occasional, which is a comparative and normative judgment their formulation does not cover. (2) NO PERSISTENCE - the loop is per-session and per-model; nothing states that answers are stored, validated, reconciled with prior answers, or reused on the next model. SQ2 is therefore untouched by this paper and remains fully open. (3) NO BURDEN MODEL - question selection maximises clarification value, but there is no cost model, no budget, no stopping rule and no reported measurement of expert effort, so 'without unnecessary expert burden' - the second half of SQ1 - is not answered. (4) NO TRANSFER CLAIM - single domain-modelling context, so SQ3 is untouched. (5) It is a 'Towards' paper on ER's LLM-enabled-modeling track, i.e. an early proposal; the thesis should verify the strength of its evaluation before conceding ground. Practical consequence: rewrite the SQ1 novelty statement to be about *governed, persistent, cost-aware* escalation over comparative judgments, and cite this paper as the nearest neighbour that establishes the escalation loop itself. Also note the co-author overlap with the conceptual-modelling establishment (Cabot, Proper) - this is the community VEGO-AI's doctorate publishes into.
sources.citation_use: RQ1 PRIMARY - nearest-neighbour prior art; supplies the rule-based-moderator + uncertainty-ranked-question mechanism, and defines the novelty boundary the thesis must argue past (persistence, burden cost model, comparative judgments, transfer).

sources.authors: Prabhsimran Singh, Younes Boubekeur, Gunter Mussbacher
sources.title: Detecting mistakes in a domain model
sources.venue: MODELS '22 Companion (25th Int. Conf. on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems: Companion Proceedings), 257-266
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL and dblp: MoDELS (Companion) 2022, pp. 257-266, DOI 10.1145/3550356.3561583. Context worth knowing: the paper was presented at the co-located 14th System Analysis and Modelling conference (SAM 2022, Montreal, Oct 2022) but is published in the MODELS Companion volume, so both venue names appear in the wild. An EXTENDED JOURNAL VERSION exists and is likely the better citation: Singh, Boubekeur, Mussbacher, 'Detecting mistakes in a domain model: a comparison of three approaches', Innovations in Systems and Software Engineering 21(3), 877-899, 2025, DOI 10.1007/s11334-024-00566-1.
sources.what_it_establishes: Automated detection of mistakes in student-produced domain models, with the extended version comparing three detection approaches head to head.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the direct antecedent of VEGO-AI's OCCASIONAL category and therefore load-bearing for SQ1. It shows that 'this element is a mistake' was already being computed automatically - pre-LLM - which sharpens what VEGO-AI actually adds: not mistake detection, but the *substantial vs occasional* discrimination, where a difference may be non-conforming yet still a legitimate alternative. For SQ1 this gives the thesis a calibrated trigger design: cases a deterministic mistake-detector already resolves should NOT be escalated to a human, and escalation budget should be spent only on the residue the detector cannot classify. That is a concrete, implementable escalation policy grounded in published baselines. The 2025 journal version's three-way comparison also supplies ready-made baseline numbers for the thesis's evaluation chapter, and its shared authorship with Mussbacher links it to reference [31].
sources.citation_use: RQ1 - baseline for automated mistake detection; defines the residue that justifies human escalation and supplies comparison baselines.

sources.authors: Christos Tselonis, John Sargeant, Mary McGee Wood
sources.title: Diagram Matching for Human-Computer Collaborative Assessment
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 9th International Computer Assisted Assessment (CAA) Conference, Loughborough University, UK, July 2005
sources.verification_note: Existence CONFIRMED: full-text PDF on the CAA conference archive (caaconference.lboro.ac.uk/pastConferences/2005/proceedings/TselonisC_SargeantJ_McGee_WoodM.pdf), a record in the Loughborough University repository (Figshare item 9488852) and a Semantic Scholar record. TWO caveats: (1) the third author's surname is 'McGee Wood' (Mary McGee Wood, University of Manchester), so the VEGO-AI reference's 'Wood, M. M.' is an incorrect name split and should be corrected to 'McGee Wood, M.'; (2) no DOI exists for this 2005 CAA paper and I could not confirm an authoritative page range - one secondary source reports 1-15, which I could not independently corroborate, so do not assert a page range without checking the PDF. The Loughborough repository page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching and the PDF could not be text-extracted in this environment.
sources.what_it_establishes: Methods for matching student-drawn diagrams against reference diagrams, applied explicitly within a HUMAN-COMPUTER COLLABORATIVE ASSESSMENT paradigm: the machine finds similarities using a simple heuristic process (reported effective) and the human marker adjudicates the rest. The same Manchester group's earlier work applied the identical collaborative division of labour to free-text marking.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Strategically the most valuable historical citation in this batch for SQ1. It proves that 'the system does what it can reliably do and routes the remainder to a human' is a twenty-year-old, named paradigm in assessment - human-computer collaborative assessment - not an artefact of the LLM era. Three uses: (1) it lets the thesis frame SQ1 as the modern, agentic instantiation of an established paradigm rather than a novelty, which is a much stronger scholarly position; (2) it supplies pre-LLM terminology (collaborative assessment, machine confidence, human adjudication) that the thesis can reuse to keep its governance vocabulary independent of any particular model generation; (3) it is a warning about a failure mode - these systems allocated work by heuristic *matching confidence*, with no representation of the marker's reasoning, so nothing was learned across cohorts. That is exactly the loss SQ2 exists to prevent, making this paper the historical evidence that escalation without judgment persistence is a known dead end. Also directly on-domain: diagrams, student work, assessment.
sources.citation_use: RQ1 - historical foundation establishing human-computer collaborative assessment as a named paradigm; also motivates SQ2 by showing escalation-without-retention loses knowledge across cohorts.

sources.authors: Yujing Yang, Boqi Chen, Kua Chen, Gunter Mussbacher, Dániel Varró
sources.title: Multi-step Iterative Automated Domain Modeling with Large Language Models
sources.venue: MODELS Companion '24 (ACM/IEEE 27th Int. Conf. on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems: Companion Proceedings), 587-595
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL: pp. 587-595, DOI 10.1145/3652620.3687807, exactly as given in the VEGO-AI reference (the only entry in this batch that already carried a DOI, and it is correct). All five authors match. A related McGill master's thesis by Yujing Yang, 'Multi-step Automated Domain Modeling with Large Language Models', is openly available via eScholarship@McGill and gives fuller methodological detail.
sources.what_it_establishes: Criticises single-shot prompting (feeding all information to the LLM in one step) and proposes a multi-step framework that extracts model elements - classes, attributes, relationships - stepwise, INJECTING INSTRUCTIONS AND HUMAN KNOWLEDGE AT EACH STEP, with an iterative pattern-identification loop and a SELF-REFLECTION mechanism that generates internal feedback and folds it back into the domain model.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Two sharp contributions to SQ2, one positive and one adversarial. Positive: 'includes instructions and human knowledge in each step' is a primitive form of exactly what SQ2 formalises - human knowledge encoded as a reusable, step-scoped artefact rather than as ad-hoc prompting. The thesis can cite it as evidence that per-step knowledge injection improves output quality, then argue the missing half is governance: their human knowledge is hard-coded prompt content with no provenance, no validation, no reconciliation when two experts disagree, and no scope-of-validity limit, so it generalises silently - the 'unsafe generalization' SQ2 names as the risk. Adversarial: the self-reflection mechanism is the strongest available claim that a system can correct itself WITHOUT a human, and it is the argument a sceptical examiner will raise against the whole doctorate. The thesis must engage it directly and show where internal feedback cannot substitute for external authority - specifically for normative judgments like substantial-vs-occasional, where there is no internal ground truth to reflect against. Also note the shared authorship with [29] (Mussbacher), so the McGill group is a coherent competing programme worth tracking.
sources.citation_use: RQ2 - prior art on injecting human knowledge into an LLM modelling pipeline, plus the self-reflection counter-argument the thesis must rebut.

sources.authors: C. K. Chow
sources.title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 16(1), 41-46
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on IEEE Xplore (document 1054406) and dblp (journals/tit/Chow70). Volume 16, issue 1, pages 41-46, 1970 all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: The original Bayes-optimal reject rule: abstain when the maximum posterior falls below a threshold, and the error-reject tradeoff curve that this induces. Establishes that the error rate can be read directly off the reject function.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the mathematical ancestor of every 'when should the system ask a human' rule the thesis will write. It gives SQ1 its canonical baseline: a single confidence threshold tuned to a target rejection rate. The thesis needs this as the strawman that a VEGO-AI intervention policy must beat, because Chow's rule assumes (a) a calibrated posterior, (b) a single scalar notion of difficulty, and (c) a fixed unit cost per rejection - all three fail for multi-agent LLM verdicts on SUBSTANTIAL vs OCCASIONAL variability, where the 'cost' is a supervisor's attention and the uncertainty is disagreement between agents rather than a posterior.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the origin of the reject-option lineage when defining the SQ1 baseline policy and when justifying why a scalar-threshold intervention rule is insufficient.

sources.authors: Ran El-Yaniv, Yair Wiener
sources.title: On the Foundations of Noise-free Selective Classification
sources.venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research, 11, 1605-1641
sources.verification_note: Full PDF confirmed on jmlr.org, volume 11, pages 1605-1641, 2010. Also indexed in ACM DL (5555/1756006.1859904).
sources.what_it_establishes: Formalises selective classification as an explicit coverage/risk tradeoff, and introduces the risk-coverage curve as the evaluation object. Gives theory for achieving a target risk at maximal coverage.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies SQ1's core EVALUATION METRIC, not just a mechanism. A selective-intervention policy for VEGO-AI can be evaluated exactly as a risk-coverage curve: x-axis = fraction of variability items handled autonomously (coverage), y-axis = error on those items. This lets the thesis report 'expert burden vs. residual error' as a single curve and compare policies by area-under-risk-coverage, which is the honest way to answer 'without unnecessary expert burden'.
sources.citation_use: Cite when defining the risk-coverage evaluation protocol for the SQ1 intervention policy and when setting a target-risk-at-fixed-coverage operating point.

sources.authors: Corinna Cortes, Giulia DeSalvo, Mehryar Mohri
sources.title: Learning with Rejection
sources.venue: Algorithmic Learning Theory (ALT 2016), LNCS, pp. 67-82, Bari, Italy
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, dblp (conf/alt/CortesDM16), ACM DL and Google Research publications page. ALT 2016, pages 67-82.
sources.what_it_establishes: Shows that the rejector should be LEARNED JOINTLY with the predictor rather than derived post-hoc from confidence, with Rademacher-complexity generalisation bounds, consistency and calibration results for the resulting surrogate losses.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ1 the key theoretical argument for treating the intervention policy as a first-class learned object with its own hypothesis class, separate from the agents that produce the verdicts. For VEGO-AI this means the escalation function can use features the classification agents never see (inter-agent disagreement, model-element type, cohort size) - and this paper is the formal warrant that doing so beats confidence thresholding.
sources.citation_use: Cite to justify architecting the intervention module as a separately parameterised rejector rather than a threshold on agent confidence.

sources.authors: Yonatan Geifman, Ran El-Yaniv
sources.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NeurIPS 2017), pp. 4878-4887
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on the NeurIPS proceedings site (paper/7073), dblp (conf/nips/GeifmanE17) and arXiv 1705.08500. Pages 4878-4887.
sources.what_it_establishes: A practical procedure (SGR) for wrapping an already-trained deep network with a selective classifier that guarantees a user-specified risk level with high probability at maximal coverage, using a held-out calibration set.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the most directly transplantable MECHANISM for SQ1: it does not require retraining the underlying model, which matters because VEGO-AI's four agents are LLM-based and effectively frozen. The thesis can adopt exactly this pattern - calibrate an escalation threshold on a labelled subset of variability items so that the residual error among auto-accepted items is provably below a level the supervisor sets. That converts 'when should we ask a human' into a governance knob an expert can actually set.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the concrete post-hoc calibration mechanism underpinning the SQ1 intervention policy and its guarantee statement.

sources.authors: David Madras, Toniann Pitassi, Richard Zemel
sources.title: Predict Responsibly: Improving Fairness and Accuracy by Learning to Defer
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31 (NeurIPS 2018), pp. 6150-6160
sources.verification_note: dblp record conf/nips/MadrasPZ18 confirms authors, NeurIPS 2018, pages 6150-6160. Note: an earlier arXiv/workshop version circulated as 'Predict Responsibly: Increasing Fairness by Learning To Defer' - cite the NeurIPS 2018 title.
sources.what_it_establishes: Distinguishes REJECTION (abstain in isolation) from DEFERRAL (abstain knowing a specific downstream decision-maker will act), and shows the optimal abstention policy changes once you model the human who receives the deferred case - including when that human is inconsistent or biased.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the conceptual pivot SQ1 depends on. The thesis is not asking 'when is the system unsure' but 'when is asking THIS expert worth THIS interruption' - which is deferral, not rejection. Madras et al. give the formal statement that the intervention rule must be conditioned on the expert's own error profile, which directly motivates the thesis's move to model supervisor competence and workload. Also gives a precedent for adversarial framing: what happens when the human is worse than the system on some items.
sources.citation_use: Cite when drawing the rejection/deferral distinction in the SQ1 problem formulation and when arguing the intervention policy must model the expert, not just the model.

sources.authors: Hussein Mozannar, David Sontag
sources.title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2020), PMLR 119, pp. 7076-7087
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on PMLR v119 (mozannar20b), ACM DL (10.5555/3524938.3525594), ICML 2020 slides, and the clinicalml/learn-to-defer GitHub repo. arXiv 2006.01862.
sources.what_it_establishes: A consistent surrogate loss for learning to defer, via reduction to cost-sensitive learning, that generalises cross-entropy - trained using only observed samples of the expert's decisions, without needing a model of the expert's internal process.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Provides the training recipe SQ1 needs given realistic data constraints: the thesis will have supervisor labels on a limited set of variability items, not a full behavioural model of the supervisor. This paper says that is enough. It also supplies the loss function that makes the learned escalation policy statistically well-behaved, which the thesis needs if it wants to claim its intervention policy is principled rather than heuristic.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the training objective for the learned escalation policy; also cite as the reference implementation baseline in SQ1 experiments.

sources.authors: Hussein Mozannar, Hunter Lang, Dennis Wei, Prasanna Sattigeri, Subhro Das, David Sontag
sources.title: Who Should Predict? Exact Algorithms For Learning to Defer to Humans
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 26th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2023), PMLR 206 (oral)
sources.verification_note: PDF confirmed on PMLR v206 (mozannar23a); companion benchmark repo clinicalml/human_ai_deferral confirms AISTATS 2023. Exact page range not recorded here - check PMLR before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: Shows prior surrogate losses can fail to find the system-optimal deferral rule, gives exact/consistent algorithms for jointly learning classifier and rejector so the AI COMPLEMENTS the human, and contributes a human-AI deferral evaluation benchmark.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Two things for SQ1. First, a correctness warning: the obvious surrogate-loss approach can be provably suboptimal, so the thesis should not casually adopt a softmax-with-defer-class design without citing this. Second, the accompanying benchmark gives a ready-made evaluation harness and set of baselines, so SQ1 can report against an established protocol rather than an ad-hoc one - useful when defending the empirical chapter.
sources.citation_use: Cite when specifying the SQ1 algorithm choice and its failure modes, and as the source of comparison baselines/benchmark protocol.

sources.authors: Kilian Hendrickx, Lorenzo Perini, Dries Van der Plas, Wannes Meert, Jesse Davis
sources.title: Machine learning with a reject option: a survey
sources.venue: Machine Learning, 113, 3073-3110
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, volume 113, pages 3073-3110, 2024. Preprint arXiv:2107.11277.
sources.what_it_establishes: Consolidated taxonomy of rejection: AMBIGUITY rejection (the item sits near a decision boundary) vs NOVELTY rejection (the item is unlike anything seen), plus architectures (separated, dependent, integrated) and training strategies for each.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ1 its organising vocabulary and, more importantly, a substantive distinction that maps onto VEGO-AI's actual problem. A domain-model difference can be escalated because the agents disagree about whether it is substantial (ambiguity) or because the construct is outside the guideline's coverage entirely (novelty). Those two demand different human questions and different downstream handling in SQ2. The survey lets the thesis define a two-channel escalation taxonomy with literature backing rather than inventing one.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the survey anchor for the SQ1 related-work section and as the source of the ambiguity/novelty escalation-type distinction.

sources.authors: Jean V. Alves, Diogo Leitão, Sérgio Jesus, Marco O. P. Sampaio, Javier Liébana, Pedro Saleiro, Mário A. T. Figueiredo, Pedro Bizarro
sources.title: Cost-Sensitive Learning to Defer to Multiple Experts with Workload Constraints
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.06906 (v3, Aug 2024)
sources.verification_note: arXiv record, title and full author list confirmed directly on arxiv.org/abs/2403.06906 (submitted 11 Mar 2024, v3 19 Aug 2024). A secondary search summary claimed publication in TMLR 2024, but the arXiv page shows NO journal reference - do not cite a TMLR venue without independently confirming it.
sources.what_it_establishes: The DeCCaF method: deferral under (a) asymmetric error costs, (b) only one human prediction available per training instance rather than all experts labelling everything, and (c) hard per-expert work-capacity limits, solved with constraint programming. Reports ~8.4% mean misclassification-cost reduction over baselines.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the closest published match to SQ1's literal phrasing - 'a BOUNDED BUDGET of expert attention'. It converts 'don't over-burden the expert' from a soft aspiration into a hard capacity constraint in the optimisation, which is exactly the governance primitive the thesis wants. Its second assumption is equally important: VEGO-AI evaluation data will have at most one expert opinion per model element, not a full expert-by-item matrix, and this paper shows deferral is still learnable in that regime.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the primary mechanism for encoding a supervisor attention budget as an explicit constraint, and for the single-expert-label training regime.

sources.authors: Giulia DeSalvo, Clara Mohri, Mehryar Mohri, Yutao Zhong
sources.title: Budgeted Multiple-Expert Deferral
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.26706 (submitted 30 Oct 2025)
sources.verification_note: Title, four authors and 30 Oct 2025 submission confirmed directly on the arXiv abstract page. Listed under cs.LG/stat.ML with no journal reference - it is a preprint; check for a peer-reviewed version before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: Attacks the TRAINING-TIME cost of deferral: standard deferral training queries every expert on every training instance. Introduces algorithms that query only a selected subset of experts per example, with generalisation bounds and label-complexity analyses, for both two-stage and single-stage multi-expert settings.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Directly addresses the most likely practical objection to SQ1 in a PhD defence: 'building your escalation policy requires more expert labelling than the escalation policy will ever save.' This paper gives the label-complexity argument that the budget applies to policy construction too, not only to deployment. For a thesis whose empirical base is a limited pool of supervisor judgments on student UML models, that is a load-bearing citation and it is very recent.
sources.citation_use: Cite when justifying the labelling budget of the SQ1 study design and when arguing the intervention policy is cheap to build, not only cheap to run.

sources.authors: Burr Settles
sources.title: Active Learning Literature Survey
sources.venue: Computer Sciences Technical Report 1648, University of Wisconsin-Madison
sources.verification_note: Confirmed in the UW-Madison MINDS institutional repository (handle 1793/60660) and cross-referenced in multiple bibliographies as Technical Report 1648, 2009.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical catalogue of query strategies - uncertainty sampling, query-by-committee, expected model change, expected error reduction, variance reduction, density-weighting - and the three query scenarios (pool-based, stream-based, membership synthesis).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the concrete menu of WHICH ITEM to escalate once SQ1 has decided that some escalation budget will be spent. Two entries matter most for VEGO-AI: query-by-committee maps almost one-to-one onto disagreement among the four VEGO-AI agents, giving a principled, pre-existing formalism for turning inter-agent disagreement into an escalation score; and density-weighting warns against escalating outliers that are unrepresentative of the cohort - important when the aim is to learn a reusable rule about substantial variability, not to adjudicate one odd student diagram.
sources.citation_use: Cite for the query-by-committee formalisation of multi-agent disagreement and for the representativeness/density correction on escalation ranking.

sources.authors: Eduardo Mosqueira-Rey, Elena Hernández-Pereira, David Alonso-Ríos, José Bobes-Bascarán, Ángel Fernández-Leal
sources.title: Human-in-the-loop machine learning: a state of the art
sources.venue: Artificial Intelligence Review, 56(4), 3005-3054
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL and the Universidade da Coruña research portal: volume 56, issue 4, pages 3005-3054. Published online 2022, issue dated 2023 - both years appear in the wild; cite 2023 with the volume/issue.
sources.what_it_establishes: Organises HITL-ML by WHO HOLDS CONTROL of the learning loop: active learning (system initiates), interactive machine learning (tight bidirectional loop), machine teaching (human domain expert initiates and controls).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives the thesis a defensible way to POSITION SQ1 rather than just cite it. The doctoral framing is deliberately not pure active learning (system decides everything) nor pure machine teaching (expert drives everything) - it is a governed middle where the system proposes escalations but the expert retains authority. This taxonomy makes that positioning legible to reviewers and exposes the gap: none of the three categories has a principled account of an ATTENTION BUDGET, which is precisely what SQ1 adds.
sources.citation_use: Cite in the SQ1 positioning paragraph to locate the thesis between active learning and machine teaching, and to state the budget gap.

sources.authors: Xingjiao Wu, Luwei Xiao, Yixuan Sun, Junhang Zhang, Tianlong Ma, Liang He
sources.title: A survey of human-in-the-loop for machine learning
sources.venue: Future Generation Computer Systems, 135, 364-381
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ScienceDirect (S0167739X22001790), ACM DL and the East China Normal University research portal: volume 135, pages 364-381, 2022.
sources.what_it_establishes: Classifies HITL work by intervention point - data processing, interventional model training, and system-independent HITL design - and frames the field's objective explicitly as reaching target accuracy at MINIMUM HUMAN COST.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The 'minimum cost' framing is the survey-level statement of SQ1's optimisation target, useful as a one-line justification that the burden question is a recognised field objective and not a private concern of this thesis. Its intervention-point taxonomy also helps the thesis be precise: VEGO-AI escalation is system-independent HITL over a frozen LLM ensemble, which rules out most of the data-processing and training-time literature and usefully narrows the related work.
sources.citation_use: Cite alongside Mosqueira-Rey to establish that minimising expert cost is a first-order field objective, and to scope SQ1 to system-independent HITL.

sources.authors: Clara Punzi, Roberto Pellungrini, Mattia Setzu, Fosca Giannotti, Dino Pedreschi
sources.title: Learning Paradigms for Hybrid Decision-Making Systems (arXiv title: AI, Meet Human: Learning Paradigms for Hybrid Decision Making Systems)
sources.venue: ACM Computing Surveys
sources.verification_note: arXiv:2402.06287 (v3, 7 Mar 2025) confirms the five authors and carries the journal reference DOI 10.1145/3802522 (ACM Computing Surveys). The ACM DL page itself returned HTTP 403 so the published title wording, volume/issue and final year could not be read directly; a search snippet indicated an April 2026 publication date and a slightly shortened title. Confirm the published title and year on ACM DL before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: A recent taxonomy of hybrid decision-making systems with explicit attention to uncertainty-driven abstention mechanisms that determine when an AI acts autonomously versus when it calls for human intervention.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most current survey that treats 'when to call the human' as the organising axis rather than an implementation detail - which is exactly SQ1's axis. Valuable for demonstrating the thesis is current with 2025/2026 literature, and for harvesting a structured gap statement: existing hybrid systems abstain per-instance and stateless, with no memory of what the expert previously ruled, which is the bridge from SQ1 into SQ2's governed knowledge reuse.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the most recent framing survey for SQ1 and as the source of the stateless-abstention gap that motivates SQ2.

sources.authors: Saurav Kadavath, Tom Conerly, Amanda Askell, Tom Henighan, Dawn Drain, Ethan Perez, Nicholas Schiefer, et al.
sources.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2207.05221 (v4, 21 Nov 2022)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on arXiv (2207.05221, v4 Nov 2022) and Semantic Scholar. Large author list (36 authors) - confirmed lead authors only. It remains a preprint, not a peer-reviewed venue paper; note this if a reviewer is strict about venues.
sources.what_it_establishes: Large models are reasonably well-calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false questions when the format is right, and can be prompted to self-evaluate (P(True)) and to predict whether they know the answer (P(IK)). Calibration degrades with format changes and on open-ended generation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the empirical licence - and the empirical limit - for using LLM self-reported confidence as the escalation trigger in an LLM-agent system like VEGO-AI. It supports a cheap first-pass signal, but its caveats (format sensitivity, weaker calibration off multiple-choice, degradation out of distribution) are precisely the reason SQ1 cannot stop at 'ask the model how sure it is'. The thesis can use it to justify a hybrid trigger: self-reported confidence plus inter-agent disagreement plus a calibrated threshold.
sources.citation_use: Cite when introducing self-reported LLM confidence as an escalation feature, and immediately after, when stating why it is insufficient alone.

sources.authors: Lorenz Kuhn, Yarin Gal, Sebastian Farquhar
sources.title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
sources.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2023), Kigali, Rwanda (oral, top 25%)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (conf/iclr/KuhnGF23), the ICLR 2023 virtual site (oral 12609) and arXiv 2302.09664.
sources.what_it_establishes: Token-level entropy misestimates uncertainty because semantically equivalent sentences are counted as distinct outcomes. Introduces semantic entropy, which clusters generations by meaning before computing entropy; unsupervised, single model, no fine-tuning, and more predictive of correctness than baselines.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Solves a problem SQ1 will hit immediately in VEGO-AI. The agents produce free-text rationales about why a model difference is substantial or occasional; two agents can express the SAME judgment in different words. A naive disagreement measure would fire a spurious escalation and waste supervisor attention. Semantic entropy gives a meaning-level agreement measure, so escalation fires on genuine substantive disagreement. Directly reduces false-positive interruptions, which is the burden half of SQ1.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the method for computing meaning-level (not surface-level) agreement among agent rationales when constructing the escalation signal.

sources.authors: Victor Quach, Adam Fisch, Tal Schuster, Adam Yala, Jae Ho Sohn, Tommi Jaakkola, Regina Barzilay
sources.title: Conformal Language Modeling
