sources.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on the ICLR 2024 proceedings site, Google Research publications page and Semantic Scholar. Author list matches.
sources.what_it_establishes: Extends conformal prediction to open-ended generation: calibrates a stopping rule for sampling LM outputs, growing a candidate set until the model is confident the set contains at least one acceptable response, with distribution-free statistical guarantees.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ1 a distribution-free GUARANTEE rather than a heuristic - the property that makes an intervention policy governable. A supervisor can set a coverage level (e.g. 90% of auto-accepted variability classifications must be acceptable) and the calibration procedure enforces it. Crucially it works for generative outputs, so it applies to VEGO-AI's natural-language verdicts and not only to closed-set labels. This is what lets the thesis state an escalation policy as an auditable contract with the expert.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the guarantee-providing calibration machinery for generative agent outputs in the SQ1 policy, and when specifying the supervisor-settable risk level.

sources.authors: Yu Gui, Ying Jin, Zhimei Ren
sources.title: Conformal Alignment: Knowing When to Trust Foundation Models with Guarantees
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2024)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on the NeurIPS 2024 proceedings site (poster 94658), OpenReview (YzyCEJlV9Z) and arXiv 2405.10301. Applications reported for question answering and radiology report generation.
sources.what_it_establishes: A framework that selects the subset of model outputs meeting a user-specified alignment criterion, guaranteeing that a prescribed fraction of SELECTED units genuinely meet it - model-agnostic and distribution-free - by training a lightweight alignment predictor on modest reference data.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Reframes SQ1 from 'reject the uncertain' to 'certify the trustworthy and route the rest to a human', which is the operationally correct direction for a guideline-operationalisation system: the expert's budget should be spent on the uncertified remainder. The 'modest reference data' requirement matches the thesis's realistic labelled-data situation. Its radiology application also gives an early, defensible bridge toward SQ3's healthcare transfer ambition without over-claiming.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the certify-then-route formulation of the SQ1 policy, and as an SQ3 transfer precedent (same machinery, software and clinical domains).

sources.authors: Allen Z. Ren, Anushri Dixit, Alexandra Bodrova, Sumeet Singh, Stephen Tu, Noah Brown, Peng Xu, Leila Takayama, Fei Xia, Jake Varley, Zhenjia Xu, Dorsa Sadigh, Andy Zeng, Anirudha Majumdar
sources.title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
sources.venue: Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2023), PMLR 229, pp. 661-682
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on PMLR v229 (ren23a, pages 661-682), dblp (conf/corl/RenDBSTBXTXVXSZ23), the Princeton research portal, arXiv 2307.01928 and the project site robot-help.github.io. Known as KnowNo.
sources.what_it_establishes: KnowNo: uses conformal prediction to calibrate an LLM planner's uncertainty so it asks a human for help exactly when needed, with a statistical guarantee on task success while MINIMISING the amount of human help requested. Works with off-the-shelf LLMs, no fine-tuning. Handles several distinct modes of ambiguity.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The single closest methodological template for SQ1. It is an LLM-agent system that explicitly trades a task-success guarantee against a help rate - the exact two-quantity tradeoff SQ1 poses, in an LLM setting, with the constraint of a frozen off-the-shelf model that VEGO-AI shares. Its treatment of distinct AMBIGUITY MODES is a directly reusable idea: escalation triggers should be typed (ambiguous guideline wording, ambiguous model construct, genuine legitimate alternative), which also feeds the SQ2 representation of what was asked and why.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the primary methodological precedent for SQ1; adopt its help-rate-versus-guarantee reporting format for the thesis's experiments.

sources.authors: Bingbing Wen, Jihan Yao, Shangbin Feng, Chenjun Xu, Yulia Tsvetkov, Bill Howe, Lucy Lu Wang
sources.title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 13, 529-556
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACL Anthology (2025.tacl-1.26), MIT Press Direct (tacl_a_00754) and arXiv 2407.18418. TACL volume 13, pages 529-556, 2025.
sources.what_it_establishes: A three-perspective framework for LLM abstention - the QUERY, the MODEL, and HUMAN VALUES - plus an organised inventory of abstention methods, benchmarks and evaluation metrics, with stated limitations of prior work.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The human-values axis is what makes this more than an uncertainty survey and is the reason it belongs in a governance thesis: it establishes in the literature that abstention is sometimes a NORMATIVE decision (this judgment should belong to a human) rather than an epistemic one (the model is unsure). SQ1 needs exactly that split, because in guideline operationalisation some variability decisions must be escalated on authority grounds even when the agents are confident. Also supplies the current metric inventory for evaluating abstention.
sources.citation_use: Cite for the epistemic-versus-normative escalation distinction in the SQ1 policy design, and as the source of candidate abstention evaluation metrics.

sources.authors: Wenxuan Wang, Juluan Shi, Zixuan Ling, Yuk-Kit Chan, Chaozheng Wang, Cheryl Lee, Youliang Yuan, Jen-tse Huang, Wenxiang Jiao, Michael R. Lyu
sources.title: Learning to Ask: When LLM Agents Meet Unclear Instruction
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2025), Suzhou, China, pp. 21773-21784
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACL Anthology (2025.emnlp-main.1104, pages 21773-21784) and arXiv 2409.00557.
sources.what_it_establishes: Documents that next-token-prediction training pushes LLM agents to FABRICATE missing arguments rather than ask, and proposes Ask-when-Needed plus the ToolEvaluator harness and Noisy ToolBench, evaluating both accuracy and interaction efficiency.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Provides the failure-mode evidence that motivates SQ1 in an agentic setting specifically: agents default to confabulating rather than escalating, so a deliberate intervention policy is a necessary engineering artefact, not an optional refinement. Its dual evaluation on accuracy AND interaction efficiency is a directly reusable evaluation design for the thesis - measuring not just whether escalation improved correctness but how many turns of expert attention it consumed.
sources.citation_use: Cite as evidence that agentic LLM systems under-ask by default, and as a template for jointly reporting accuracy and interaction cost in SQ1 evaluation.

sources.authors: Anna M. Wundram, Christian F. Baumgartner
sources.title: Is Uncertainty Quantification a Viable Alternative to Learned Deferral?
sources.venue: MICCAI 2025 UNSURE workshop (Uncertainty for Safe Utilization of Machine Learning in Medical Imaging), oral
sources.verification_note: arXiv 2508.02319 confirmed; ACM DL record 10.1007/978-3-032-06593-3_4 confirms publication in the UNSURE workshop proceedings volume. Accepted as an oral at MICCAI UNSURE 2025.
sources.what_it_establishes: Head-to-head comparison of the two escalation paradigms - learned deferral (supervised, trained on the deployment distribution) versus threshold-on-uncertainty-quantification - finding UQ methods more robust under distribution shift and out-of-distribution input.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Answers a design question SQ1 must answer explicitly and gives an empirically grounded default. Learned deferral is trained on a specific distribution of variability items; the thesis's whole SQ3 ambition is transfer to new guideline-operationalisation contexts, i.e. deliberate distribution shift. This paper says the learned-deferral route degrades exactly there. It therefore supplies the justification for a UQ-based or hybrid escalation trigger and creates a concrete, testable hypothesis linking SQ1 design choices to SQ3 transfer outcomes.
sources.citation_use: Cite when justifying the choice between learned-deferral and UQ-threshold escalation, and when linking SQ1 mechanism choice to SQ3 transfer robustness.

sources.authors: Heleen van der Sijs, Jos Aarts, Arnold Vulto, Marc Berg
sources.title: Overriding of Drug Safety Alerts in Computerized Physician Order Entry
sources.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association, 13(2), 138-147
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on PubMed (16357358), Oxford Academic JAMIA (13(2):138-147, March 2006), ScienceDirect and the Erasmus University repository. 17 included studies.
sources.what_it_establishes: Systematic review finding clinicians override drug safety alerts in 49% to 96% of cases, and attributing this to error-producing conditions in the alerting system itself: low specificity, low sensitivity, unclear information content, and unnecessary workflow disruption.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is SQ1's empirical warning from the only field with decades of deployed selective-intervention systems. It converts 'unnecessary expert burden' from an abstract cost into a documented failure mode with quantified consequences: escalate too often with too little specificity and the expert stops engaging, which destroys the value of the human judgment SQ2 is meant to capture. It also gives the thesis a concrete list of what makes an intervention BAD (specificity, information content, workflow timing) - a ready-made design checklist for VEGO-AI escalation prompts.
sources.citation_use: Cite in the SQ1 motivation to establish the cost of over-escalation empirically, and as the source of the escalation-quality design criteria.

sources.authors: Jessica S. Ancker, Alison Edwards, Sarah Nosal, Diane Hauser, Elizabeth Mauer, Rainu Kaushal (with the HITEC Investigators)
sources.title: Effects of workload, work complexity, and repeated alerts on alert fatigue in a clinical decision support system
sources.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making, 17, Article 36
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on SpringerLink, PubMed (28395667) and PMC (PMC5387195). Retrospective cohort, 112 ambulatory primary care clinicians, EHR data Jan 2010-Jun 2013. Note a published correction exists (PubMed 31739801, PMC6859609).
sources.what_it_establishes: Empirically separates two mechanisms of alert fatigue - cognitive overload (from work volume, complexity, and difficulty telling informative from uninformative alerts) and desensitisation (from repeated exposure to the same alert over time) - using longitudinal clinician-level data.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ1 a STATE-DEPENDENT cost model, which is the piece missing from the entire learning-to-defer literature. The cost of an escalation is not constant: it rises with the expert's current load and with how many times that same escalation type has already been shown. That means the optimal intervention policy must be adaptive over a review session, not a fixed threshold. This is a genuine, citable gap the thesis can claim - combining a formal deferral budget with an empirically grounded, time-varying interruption cost is not something the deferral papers do.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the empirical basis for a time-varying/adaptive escalation cost, and as the gap statement distinguishing SQ1's contribution from static deferral budgets.

sources.authors: Ben Green, Yiling Chen
sources.title: The Principles and Limits of Algorithm-in-the-Loop Decision Making
sources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction, 3(CSCW)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on dblp (journals/pacmhci/GreenC19), Harvard Scholar and Semantic Scholar. Authors are Ben Green and Yiling Chen. Exact article number and page range not recorded here - retrieve from dblp/ACM before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: Empirically shows people do not collaborate with algorithms the way normative accounts assume - people cannot reliably evaluate algorithmic predictions, do not correctly calibrate their reliance, and society lacks clear normative principles for what good human-algorithm collaboration even means.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Constrains what SQ1 is allowed to claim. Escalating to a human only improves the outcome if the human actually adds signal on the escalated items; this paper is the evidence that this cannot be assumed. It forces SQ1 to include a validation step measuring whether expert intervention on escalated variability items measurably improves classification, and it supports the thesis's move to GOVERNED judgment (structured, validated, recorded) rather than raw human override - which is the handoff into SQ2.
sources.citation_use: Cite when stating the assumption that escalation improves outcomes must be tested, not assumed, and to motivate governance of the judgment rather than mere human-in-the-loop.

sources.authors: Gagan Bansal, Tongshuang Wu, Joyce Zhou, Raymond Fok, Besmira Nushi, Ece Kamar, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Daniel S. Weld
sources.title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2021 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2021), Yokohama, Japan
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on ACM DL (10.1145/3411764.3445717), the UW IDL copy of the CHI paper and the NSF public access repository. Mixed-method user studies on three datasets.
sources.what_it_establishes: AI augmentation produced complementary team improvement, but explanations did NOT further increase it - explanations tended to increase acceptance of AI recommendations regardless of correctness rather than improve discrimination.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: A precise negative result that shapes SQ1's escalation interface. The intuitive design - escalate the item and attach the agents' rationale so the expert can judge - risks anchoring the expert on the AI's position, contaminating exactly the human judgment SQ2 wants to capture and reuse. The thesis should therefore treat WHAT IS SHOWN at escalation as a controlled design variable with its own evaluation, and this paper is the citation that makes that a considered decision rather than an oversight.
sources.citation_use: Cite when designing and justifying the escalation prompt/interface, and when arguing for measuring anchoring effects on captured expert judgments.

sources.authors: Ben Green
sources.title: The flaws of policies requiring human oversight of government algorithms
sources.venue: Computer Law & Security Review, volume 45
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on Harvard Scholar, SSRN (abstract 3921216), Semantic Scholar and arXiv 2109.05067. Computer Law & Security Review, volume 45, 2022. Article number not recorded here - retrieve from the publisher before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: Surveys 41 policies mandating human oversight of government algorithms and identifies two structural flaws: people cannot in practice perform the oversight functions the policies assume, and the oversight requirement legitimises deployment of faulty systems without fixing them. Argues for institutional rather than individual oversight.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The strongest available statement of the GAP that the doctoral umbrella question addresses. Regulation mandates human oversight; this paper shows the mandate is routinely hollow because it specifies that a human must be present, not WHEN the human should be engaged or with what capacity. SQ1 is a direct technical response - a principled, budgeted, auditable answer to when engagement actually happens - and Green's shift toward institutional oversight foreshadows SQ2's governed reuse of judgment as an institutional memory rather than an individual act.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the governance-side gap statement opening the SQ1 chapter, and to distinguish meaningful engagement from nominal human-in-the-loop compliance.

sources.authors: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 14 - Human oversight
sources.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, OJ L, 2024/1689, 12 July 2024
sources.verification_note: Official consolidated text confirmed on EUR-Lex (OJ L_202401689). Article 14 text on human oversight cross-checked against artificialintelligenceact.eu and aiact-info.eu mirrors. Regulation dated 13 June 2024.
sources.what_it_establishes: Legally requires high-risk AI systems to be designed so natural persons can EFFECTIVELY oversee them, with oversight measures COMMENSURATE with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use, and with overseers enabled to understand the system's capacities and limitations and to detect anomalies.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the normative mandate that makes SQ1 more than an efficiency exercise, and - critically - the word 'commensurate' is a legal requirement for PROPORTIONATE, risk-calibrated oversight, which is precisely a selective intervention policy. The thesis can position SQ1 as an operationalisation of Article 14: turning an unquantified legal obligation into a measurable escalation policy with a stated coverage guarantee and a bounded attention budget. It also frames the healthcare arm of SQ3, since clinical decision support falls under the high-risk regime.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the regulatory grounding for proportionate, risk-calibrated human engagement in the SQ1 problem statement, and for the high-risk framing of the SQ3 healthcare extension.

sources.authors: Paul F. Christiano, Jan Leike, Tom B. Brown, Miljan Martic, Shane Legg, Dario Amodei
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NeurIPS 2017), pp. 4299-4307
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM DL (NeurIPS'17 proceedings, pages 4299-4307), Google Scholar author record for Christiano, and BibSonomy. Author list, title, year and venue all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical formulation of learning a reward model from pairwise human preference comparisons over trajectory segments, then optimising a policy against that learned reward - solving complex RL tasks with feedback on ~0.1% of agent interactions.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the primary CONTRAST pole for SQ2. It defines the dominant paradigm for 'using human judgment': the judgment is consumed as scalar preference signal, compressed into reward-model weights, and thereafter uninspectable, unattributable and non-revocable. SQ2's claim - that expert judgment must be represented as a first-class, inspectable, provenance-bearing artefact - is only well-motivated if the thesis can state precisely what this paradigm gives up. It also supplies the efficiency baseline SQ1/SQ2 must beat or reframe: preference learning is sample-efficient but assumes cheap, fungible, anonymous labellers, which is exactly the assumption that fails for scarce modelling/domain experts adjudicating SUBSTANTIAL vs OCCASIONAL variability.
sources.citation_use: Cite when introducing the 'weights absorb feedback' baseline and when arguing that VEGO-AI expert judgment cannot be reduced to preference pairs.

sources.authors: Long Ouyang, Jeffrey Wu, Xu Jiang, Diogo Almeida, Carroll L. Wainwright, Pamela Mishkin, Chong Zhang, Sandhini Agarwal, Katarina Slama, Alex Ray, et al.
sources.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), pp. 27730-27744
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Semantic Scholar record and arXiv 2203.02155; NeurIPS vol. 35, pp. 27730-27744 consistently reported. Full author list is long (20 authors); I have listed the leading authors and confirmed Ouyang and Wu as first two.
sources.what_it_establishes: The three-stage RLHF pipeline at LLM scale (SFT on labeller demonstrations -> reward model from labeller rankings -> PPO), showing a 1.3B RLHF-tuned model preferred over 175B GPT-3.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the operational reference implementation of the contrast pole, and crucially it is the one that documents the human side: labeller recruitment, screening, agreement rates and the labelling instructions. For SQ2 it is a double resource - (a) it shows expert judgment being irreversibly baked into weights with no mechanism to inspect which labeller decision produced which behaviour, no reconciliation of disagreeing labellers beyond aggregation, and no revocation path; (b) its reported inter-labeller agreement figures give the thesis a concrete number to argue that disagreement was real and was thrown away. The thesis can position governed knowledge reuse as 'InstructGPT's labeller judgments, but kept as retrievable, attributable, contestable records instead of gradient updates'.
sources.citation_use: Cite for the reference RLHF pipeline and for the documented-but-discarded labeller disagreement that motivates SQ2's reconciliation requirement.

sources.authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Sandipan Kundu, Amanda Askell, Jackson Kernion, Andy Jones, Anna Chen, Anna Goldie, Azalia Mirhoseini, Cameron McKinnon, et al.
sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2212.08073 (Anthropic; not peer-reviewed)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed on arXiv (2212.08073), Semantic Scholar and Hugging Face Papers. Note this is an arXiv technical report, NOT a peer-reviewed conference/journal paper - cite it as such.
sources.what_it_establishes: Replaces per-instance human harmlessness labels with a short written list of principles (a 'constitution'); the model self-critiques and revises against those principles, and RLAIF trains a preference model from AI-generated preferences.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The single most important PARTIAL-ALIGNMENT source for SQ2, and the closest existing thing to 'governed knowledge reuse'. It is the one mainstream system where human judgment is stored in an explicit, human-readable, editable artefact (the principles) rather than only in weights - which is exactly SQ2's representation move. But it is also the sharpest CONTRAST: the constitution is a small, static, global, hand-authored document with no provenance per principle, no validation that a principle is correct for a given case, no reconciliation procedure when principles conflict, and no case-level grounding - and once RLAIF has run, the resulting behaviour is again in the weights. SQ2 must show it goes beyond CAI on four axes: case-grounded rather than global, provenance-bearing rather than anonymous, reconciled rather than hand-authored, and revocable rather than baked in. This paper is the strongest 'why isn't this already solved?' challenge a viva committee will raise.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the nearest prior art for explicit stored judgment, then use its four limitations to carve out SQ2's contribution.

sources.authors: Stephen Casper, Xander Davies, Claudia Shi, Thomas Krendl Gilbert, Jeremy Scheurer, Javier Rando, Rachel Freedman, Tomasz Korbak, et al. (33 authors)
sources.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
sources.venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 2023
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 2307.15217, Semantic Scholar, BibBase and NASA ADS; TMLR 2023 publication confirmed. Large author list (~33); leading authors listed.
sources.what_it_establishes: A systematic taxonomy of RLHF's failure modes, separating tractable problems from fundamental limitations, and explicitly calls for auditing, transparency and documentation standards around human feedback.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the paper that lets the thesis criticise RLHF without appearing to attack a strawman - it is a peer-reviewed, heavily co-authored critique from inside the alignment community. Directly supplies SQ2's problem statement: it names the difficulty of getting quality feedback from scarce/misaligned humans, the loss of information in aggregating disagreeing evaluators, the opacity of the reward model, and the absence of audit trails. Its own recommendation - that human feedback processes need documentation and external scrutiny - is essentially an unmet requirement that SQ2 proposes to meet with a governed judgment store. Use it to convert 'weights absorb feedback, uninspectable' from an assertion into a cited, community-recognised open problem.
sources.citation_use: Cite in the gap analysis as the authoritative statement that RLHF's opacity and feedback-governance problems are open, not solved.

sources.authors: Luc Moreau, Paolo Missier (editors); Khalid Belhajjame, Reza B'Far, James Cheney, Sam Coppens, Stephen Cresswell, Yolanda Gil, Paul Groth, et al.
sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.venue: W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013 (World Wide Web Consortium)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed directly at w3.org/TR/prov-dm/ - W3C Recommendation dated 30 April 2013, edited by Luc Moreau and Paolo Missier. Companion PROV-O ontology also a Recommendation of the same date. Note: this is a standards document with editors rather than conventional authors - cite accordingly.
sources.what_it_establishes: The international standard conceptual model for provenance: the Entity / Activity / Agent triad plus relations (wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf), explicitly framed around deciding whether information should be trusted.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The off-the-shelf formal backbone for SQ2's 'how should expert judgment be represented and stored'. Every judgment record the thesis proposes - an expert ruling that a given UML difference is SUBSTANTIAL, the agent reasoning that prompted the escalation, the reconciliation of two conflicting rulings - maps cleanly onto PROV: the ruling is an Entity generated by an adjudication Activity, attributed to a human Agent, derived from a prior model-comparison Entity. Adopting PROV-DM rather than inventing a bespoke schema buys the thesis standards compliance, tool interoperability, and a principled answer to 'why this representation?'. It also gives SQ3 its transfer story: provenance-typed judgment records are domain-neutral, so a software-modelling judgment store and a clinical one share vocabulary. The gap PROV does NOT cover, and which SQ2 must add, is validity/authority semantics - PROV records who said what and when, but has no notion of whether a stored judgment is still endorsed, whether it may be generalised beyond its originating case, or when it must be retired.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the adopted representational foundation, and immediately state the endorsement/scope-of-reuse gap that SQ2 extends it with.

sources.authors: Renan Souza, Leonardo Guerreiro Azevedo, Vitor Lourenco, Elton F. S. Soares, Raphael Melo Thiago, Rafael Brandao, Daniel Civitarese, Emilio Vital Brazil, Marcio Ferreira Moreno, Patrick Valduriez, Marta Mattoso, Renato Cerqueira, Marco Aurelio Stelmar Netto
sources.title: Provenance Data in the Machine Learning Lifecycle in Computational Science and Engineering
sources.venue: 2019 IEEE/ACM Workflows in Support of Large-Scale Science (WORKS), held with SC19
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 1910.04223 and Semantic Scholar; IEEE/ACM WORKS 2019 venue confirmed. Full 13-author list obtained from the arXiv record.
sources.what_it_establishes: PROV-ML: a concrete provenance representation for the ML lifecycle built by specialising W3C PROV and ML Schema, with multi-workflow provenance capture and a standard query vocabulary.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Proves the specific move SQ2 needs is feasible and has precedent: you can extend W3C PROV into a domain-specific lifecycle vocabulary and still get standards-conformant, queryable provenance. It gives the thesis a methodological template (specialise PROV rather than replace it) and a citable design precedent for a 'PROV-Judgment' or similar profile covering expert rulings in agentic assessment. The CONTRAST worth naming: PROV-ML tracks artefacts and computational steps - datasets, hyperparameters, models - and treats humans only as workflow-triggering agents; it has no vocabulary for the content of a human judgment, its rationale, its scope of applicability, or its adjudication against a competing judgment. That absence is precisely SQ2's target.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the template for extending PROV to a lifecycle, and as evidence that current ML provenance covers artefacts but not human judgment content.

sources.authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Kuettler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktaeschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020), pp. 9459-9474
sources.verification_note: Confirmed at the official NeurIPS 2020 proceedings page, dblp (conf/nips/LewisPPPKGKLYR020) and UCL Discovery. Full 12-author list, title, venue and pages all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Couples a parametric generator with a non-parametric, indexed external memory retrieved at inference time; the paper explicitly motivates this by parametric models' inability to provide provenance for decisions or to have their world knowledge updated.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The mechanism that makes SQ2 technically realisable, and the pivot away from the RLHF pole. RAG's own stated motivation - provenance and updatability - is SQ2's motivation almost verbatim, which is a strong rhetorical asset. It gives the thesis the architectural answer to 'how is stored judgment actually reused': index the judgment records, retrieve the ones relevant to the current variability case, condition the agent on them, and keep a pointer back to the originating expert ruling. Editing or withdrawing a judgment then means editing an index entry, not retraining - which is exactly what makes revocation and human authority preservable. The CONTRAST/limitation SQ2 must address: RAG retrieves on semantic similarity alone, with no notion of whether a retrieved precedent is authorised for the current context. Similarity-based retrieval of an expert ruling into a case it was never meant to govern IS the unsafe generalization failure mode named in SQ2 and SQ3, so the thesis needs governed retrieval, not plain RAG.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the reuse mechanism, then argue that ungoverned similarity retrieval is itself the unsafe-generalization risk SQ2 must control.

sources.authors: Joon Sung Park, Joseph C. O'Brien, Carrie J. Cai, Meredith Ringel Morris, Percy Liang, Michael S. Bernstein
sources.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.venue: UIST '23: Proceedings of the 36th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, Article 2, pp. 1-22
sources.verification_note: Confirmed at ACM DL (DOI 10.1145/3586183.3606763), UIST '23, San Francisco, 29 Oct - 1 Nov 2023. Author list, title, venue and pagination match.
sources.what_it_establishes: An agent memory architecture with three components - a time-stamped memory stream of natural-language observations, a retrieval function scoring recency/importance/relevance, and reflection that synthesises higher-level abstractions from stored observations - validated by ablation showing each component is necessary.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most directly transferable memory design for SQ2, and the source of its central danger. The memory stream gives a concrete pattern for storing judgment as time-stamped natural-language records with retrieval scoring - a ready starting schema for a judgment store, and the importance term is a natural hook for SQ1's escalation signals. The critical contribution to SQ2 is REFLECTION as a named CONTRAST: reflection is precisely automated generalization from stored records into new abstract beliefs, performed with no human validation, no provenance link binding the abstraction to the observations that produced it, and no gate on scope. That is the unsafe-generalization mechanism SQ2 exists to govern. The thesis can define its contribution sharply as 'reflection with a governance gate': synthesised generalizations from expert judgments are provisional, carry provenance to their source rulings, and require human endorsement before they may influence assessment. Also note the ablation methodology as a template for evaluating whether SQ2's governance components each earn their place.
sources.citation_use: Cite for the memory-stream/retrieval schema AND as the canonical example of ungoverned reflection that SQ2 must constrain.

sources.authors: Charles Packer, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Kevin Lin, Sarah Wooders, Joseph E. Gonzalez
sources.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.08560 (UC Berkeley; also indexed in dblp as CoRR abs/2310.08560)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 2310.08560 (12 Oct 2023), dblp CoRR record, Hugging Face Papers and research.memgpt.ai. This is a preprint/tech report - I did not find a peer-reviewed conference version, so cite it as arXiv.
sources.what_it_establishes: Virtual context management by analogy to OS hierarchical memory: an explicit tiered store (in-context 'main' memory vs out-of-context 'external' memory) with the LLM issuing its own function calls to page information in and out and to write persistent records.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the storage-tier engineering vocabulary SQ2 needs to answer 'how should judgment be stored' at system level rather than schema level. The main/external split maps onto a governance distinction the thesis can make its own: which expert rulings are currently in force and loaded into the agent's active reasoning context versus which are archived precedent retrievable on demand - and, critically, who is authorised to promote a record between those tiers. Self-directed paging is simultaneously the CONTRAST: MemGPT lets the model decide unilaterally what to remember, what to forget and what to write back, which under SQ2 would mean an agent silently editing the record of human judgment. SQ2's governed alternative is that write and eviction operations on the judgment store are privileged and auditable, not model-discretionary.
sources.citation_use: Cite for tiered memory architecture and self-editing memory, then contrast with SQ2's requirement that judgment writes be privileged and logged.

sources.authors: Zeyu Zhang, Xiaohe Bo, Chen Ma, Rui Li, Xu Chen, Quanyu Dai, Jieming Zhu, Zhenhua Dong, Ji-Rong Wen
sources.title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents
sources.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2404.13501
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 2404.13501 (21 April 2024) and Hugging Face Papers. Preprint - no peer-reviewed venue found, cite as arXiv.
sources.what_it_establishes: A systematic taxonomy of LLM-agent memory covering sources, forms, and the memory operations of writing, management and reading, together with evaluation approaches and open problems.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The efficient way for the thesis to demonstrate coverage of the agent-memory literature without citing dozens of individual systems, and - more usefully - to run a structured gap argument. Take the survey's own operational taxonomy (write / manage / read) and show that across the surveyed systems none of these operations carries a governance predicate: nothing in the taxonomy asks who authorised a write, whether a managed/consolidated memory retains provenance to its sources, or whether a read is permitted for the current context. Stating the gap against a published taxonomy rather than against a hand-picked set of systems makes SQ2's novelty claim considerably more defensible.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the systematic-coverage anchor for agent memory and as the frame for SQ2's 'no governance predicates on memory operations' gap claim.

sources.authors: Lora Aroyo, Chris Welty
sources.title: Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation
sources.venue: AI Magazine, 36(1), pp. 15-24
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via AAAI OJS (article 2564), Wiley Online Library, and the VU Amsterdam research portal. Authors, year, journal, volume/issue and pages all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Dismantles seven assumptions underpinning single-gold-standard annotation (one truth, one right answer per example, disagreement equals error, etc.) and proposes 'crowd truth' - that disagreement across annotators is signal about genuine interpretive ambiguity, not noise to be averaged away.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The theoretical licence for SQ2 to store disagreement rather than resolve it away, and it maps with unusual precision onto the VEGO-AI setting. VEGO-AI's SUBSTANTIAL vs OCCASIONAL distinction is exactly a claim that some variation is legitimate alternative interpretation while other variation is error - which is Aroyo and Welty's core thesis restated in the domain-modelling domain. That gives the thesis a strong conceptual bridge: 'substantial variability' in domain models is the modelling analogue of 'crowd truth' in annotation. Practically, it forbids the naive design in which conflicting expert rulings are collapsed by majority vote before storage, and instead requires SQ2's store to retain each expert's ruling with its rationale and identity, marking whether a conflict is genuine interpretive plurality (preserve both) or one expert's error (adjudicate and retire one). That distinction is the reconciliation problem SQ2 names.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the foundational justification that disagreement is signal, and to link crowd truth to the SUBSTANTIAL/OCCASIONAL distinction inherited from VEGO-AI.

sources.authors: Ron Artstein, Massimo Poesio
sources.title: Survey Article: Inter-Coder Agreement for Computational Linguistics
sources.venue: Computational Linguistics, 34(4), pp. 555-596
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACL Anthology (J08-4004), ACM DL (10.1162/coli.07-034-R2) and Semantic Scholar. Volume 34, issue 4, pp. 555-596, 2008 - all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: The definitive methodological treatment of agreement coefficients - Scott's pi, Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha, weighted variants - with their underlying assumptions made explicit, and argues weighted alpha-like coefficients often suit annotation tasks better than kappa-like ones.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The measurement instrument SQ2 needs and the source that stops the thesis using it naively. Any empirical claim about expert judgment in this PhD - that two modelling experts agree on SUBSTANTIAL vs OCCASIONAL, that the agentic system's rulings align with expert rulings, that a reconciled judgment record is stable across experts - requires a defensible agreement statistic, and this is the paper that specifies which coefficient is appropriate and what each one assumes about annotator interchangeability and category prevalence. It is also the corrective to a real methodological trap: reporting a single kappa over SUBSTANTIAL/OCCASIONAL would presuppose exactly the single-gold-standard framing that the Aroyo and Welty line rejects. Artstein and Poesio's weighted and multi-coder machinery lets the thesis quantify agreement while still treating structured disagreement as meaningful. Directly load-bearing for the empirical protocol behind the EXP-005-style labelling work.
sources.citation_use: Cite in the methodology chapter to justify the chosen agreement coefficient and its assumptions for expert variability labelling.

sources.authors: Aida Mostafazadeh Davani, Mark Diaz, Vinodkumar Prabhakaran
sources.title: Dealing with Disagreements: Looking Beyond the Majority Vote in Subjective Annotations
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL), 10, pp. 92-110
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACL Anthology (2022.tacl-1.6), MIT Press Direct (10.1162/tacl_a_00449) and transacl.org. Authors, year, volume and pages all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: A multi-task architecture that predicts each annotator's judgment as a separate head over a shared representation instead of aggregating to one label, matching or beating majority-vote training across seven binary tasks, and showing annotator disagreement is systematic rather than random.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Moves SQ2's disagreement argument from principle to engineering evidence: it demonstrates empirically that preserving per-annotator judgment costs nothing in performance and preserves information that aggregation destroys. That is the answer to the obvious reviewer objection 'why not just take the majority ruling from your experts and store one clean label?'. The finding that disagreement is systematic and traceable to individual annotators' perspectives directly supports SQ2's requirement that stored judgment be attributed to an identified expert rather than to an anonymous consensus - which is also what makes the PROV attribution relations meaningful rather than decorative. Note the CONTRAST though: Davani et al. still absorb per-annotator judgment into model parameters (one head per annotator), so the individual judgment remains uninspectable at the record level. SQ2 keeps the per-expert distinction at the level of stored, retrievable records instead.
sources.citation_use: Cite as empirical proof that preserving per-expert judgment is not costly, and to justify per-expert attribution in the judgment store.

sources.authors: Alexandra N. Uma, Tommaso Fornaciari, Dirk Hovy, Silviu Paun, Barbara Plank, Massimo Poesio
sources.title: Learning from Disagreement: A Survey
sources.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research (JAIR), 72, pp. 1385-1470
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via JAIR (article 12752), ACM DL, and the Utrecht University and IT-University of Copenhagen research portals. Volume 72, pp. 1385-1470, published 27 Dec 2021 - all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Comprehensive survey of evidence for annotator disagreement across NLP and CV tasks and of the methods for training and evaluating models on data with multiple potentially conflicting judgments, spanning objective through highly subjective tasks.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The single citation that establishes disagreement-aware learning as a mature research area rather than a niche position, which matters because SQ2's whole premise is that expert judgment is plural and must be reconciled rather than averaged. It gives the thesis a menu of existing reconciliation and aggregation strategies (probabilistic aggregation models, soft labels, multi-annotator learning) against which the proposed governance approach can be positioned and, where appropriate, adopted for the reconciliation step. It also supplies a defensible claim about task subjectivity gradients - useful for arguing that judging whether a UML difference is SUBSTANTIAL sits in the moderately-subjective band where disagreement is expected and informative, which in turn justifies SQ1's escalation triggers firing on disagreement-prone cases.
sources.citation_use: Cite to establish disagreement-aware methods as an established field and to survey candidate reconciliation strategies for SQ2.

sources.authors: Federico Cabitza, Andrea Campagner, Valerio Basile
sources.title: Toward a Perspectivist Turn in Ground Truthing for Predictive Computing
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 37th AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-23), pp. 6860-6868
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via AAAI-23 proceedings listing (pp. 6860-6868, Washington DC, Feb 2023), researchr publication record, and arXiv 2109.04270. Note the arXiv preprint dates from 2021 while the AAAI publication is 2023 - cite the AAAI version.
sources.what_it_establishes: Argues for 'data perspectivism' as a paradigm: ground truth datasets should integrate and retain the multiple perspectives of human annotators rather than collapsing them into a single gold standard via majority voting.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most recent peer-reviewed statement of the position SQ2 depends on, and the best one for the thesis to cite because Cabitza and Campagner work substantially in medical AI - which makes it a natural bridge to SQ3's healthcare transfer ambition. Where Aroyo and Welty give the conceptual argument and Uma et al. survey the methods, this paper gives a normative programme for how datasets and knowledge artefacts should be constructed, which is precisely the level at which SQ2 operates: it is a claim about representation and storage, not about model training. The thesis can position the governed judgment store as a perspectivist knowledge artefact for guideline operationalization - retaining which expert held which position on a variability decision and why - and cite this as the paradigm it instantiates. The gap it leaves open, and SQ2's contribution, is that perspectivism says retain the perspectives but says nothing about authorising, scoping or retiring them for downstream reuse.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the paradigm statement for perspectivist knowledge representation, and as the software-to-healthcare conceptual bridge toward SQ3.

sources.authors: Lucas Bourtoule, Varun Chandrasekaran, Christopher A. Choquette-Choo, Hengrui Jia, Adelin Travers, Baiwu Zhang, David Lie, Nicolas Papernot
sources.title: Machine Unlearning
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P / Oakland) 2021
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the University of Toronto authors' publication page, Semantic Scholar, and the IEEE S&P 2021 programme. Full 8-author list and venue confirmed. I did not independently confirm the exact page range, so it is omitted rather than guessed.
sources.what_it_establishes: Formalises the unlearning problem - removing a data point's influence from a trained model - and introduces SISA (Sharded, Isolated, Sliced, Aggregated) training, which limits each data point's influence in advance so that retraining on removal is bounded rather than full.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The decisive technical evidence for SQ2's revocation requirement, and the sharpest quantitative form of the contrast with RLHF. Withdrawing a piece of expert judgment from a system that absorbed it into weights is not a delete operation - it is an open research problem requiring either full retraining or a purpose-built architecture designed for removal from the outset. That single fact carries a large share of SQ2's argument: if a domain expert's ruling on variability is later found wrong, superseded by a revised guideline, or issued outside their authority, a weights-based system cannot cleanly retract it, whereas a governed record store retracts it by invalidating a record and re-running retrieval. SISA's design principle - constrain influence at write time so removal is tractable later - is itself a transferable governance idea: SQ2 can scope each stored judgment's sphere of influence at the moment it is recorded, making revocation and scope-limitation the same mechanism.
sources.citation_use: Cite to prove that revocation from weights is hard, establishing why SQ2 stores judgment externally; also cite SISA's bounded-influence principle as a design analogue.

sources.authors: Sijia Liu, Yuanshun Yao, Jinghan Jia, Stephen Casper, Nathalie Baracaldo, Peter Hase, Xiaojun Xu, Yuguang Yao, Chris Yuhao Liu, Hang Li, Kush R. Varshney, Mohit Bansal, Sanmi Koyejo, Yang Liu
sources.title: Rethinking machine unlearning for large language models
sources.venue: Nature Machine Intelligence, 7(2), pp. 181-194
sources.verification_note: Confirmed at nature.com (s42256-025-00985-0), Nature Machine Intelligence vol. 7(2):181-194, 2025, plus the NSF Public Access Repository and arXiv 2402.08787 preprint. Author list and metadata match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Reframes unlearning specifically for LLMs - unlearning scope, data-model interaction, and multifaceted efficacy assessment - and highlights that the boundaries of what has actually been removed are poorly defined and hard to verify in large models.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Updates the revocation argument to the LLM/agentic era, which the thesis needs because VEGO-AI is built on LLM agents and a reviewer will ask whether unlearning has since made weight-based retraction practical. The answer this paper supports is no: for LLMs, even determining the SCOPE of what must be unlearned, and verifying that it was, remain open. That is a governance-grade objection, not merely an efficiency one - a system that cannot demonstrate a withdrawn expert ruling no longer influences its outputs cannot claim to preserve human authority. The paper's emphasis on unlearning scope also gives SQ2 useful conceptual vocabulary: scope is exactly what an externally stored judgment record can declare explicitly and a weight update cannot.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the current state of the art showing LLM unlearning remains unverifiable, closing the revocation argument for SQ2.

sources.authors: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov
sources.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed at the official NeurIPS 2022 proceedings page, arXiv 2202.05262, the Technion research portal and the authors' GitHub (kmeng01/rome). Authors, title, year and venue match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Uses causal tracing to localise factual associations to mid-layer feed-forward modules and introduces ROME (Rank-One Model Editing) to directly modify weights so as to update a specific fact without full retraining.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The strongest competing answer to SQ2 that the thesis must confront head-on: if stored knowledge can be surgically located and edited inside the weights, one might argue governed reuse can be done parametrically after all. Including it is what makes SQ2's argument honest rather than a convenient dichotomy. The rebuttal the thesis can then mount is specific and defensible - model editing changes what the system outputs but produces no record of who authorised the edit, on what rationale, with what scope, or how it relates to prior conflicting rulings; edits are known to have unpredictable ripple effects on related facts; and there is no adjudication or contest path for a stakeholder who disagrees with an edit. In SQ2 terms, model editing addresses updatability but not governance, provenance, reconciliation or authority. Also useful as evidence that the field itself recognises the retrain-to-update problem as unacceptable, which corroborates SQ2's framing.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the parametric alternative to external judgment storage, then show it delivers updatability without provenance, adjudication or authority.

sources.authors: Agnar Aamodt, Enric Plaza
sources.title: Case-Based Reasoning: Foundational Issues, Methodological Variations, and System Approaches
sources.venue: AI Communications, 7(1), pp. 39-59
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM DL, the IIIA-CSIC copy hosted by co-author Enric Plaza, and multiple bibliographic records. AI Communications 7(1):39-59, 1994 - all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical CBR framework, including the R4 cycle - Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain - and the treatment of a case base as an evolving, sustained-learning memory of concrete prior episodes with their solutions and outcomes.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The classical precedent that gives SQ2 an intellectual lineage and a ready-made process model, which is valuable for a thesis that must justify why case-grounded reuse is principled rather than an ad hoc engineering choice. The R4 cycle maps almost one-to-one onto the governed reuse loop the thesis needs: Retrieve the relevant prior expert rulings for the current variability case, Reuse them to inform the agentic assessment, Revise where the new case differs, Retain the outcome as a new governed record. CBR also anticipates SQ2's core safety concern under its own terminology - case adaptation and similarity assessment are precisely where CBR systems generalise beyond warrant, and the CBR literature's insistence on explicit similarity metrics and adaptation knowledge is an argument that these decisions should be declared and inspectable rather than left implicit in an embedding space. Positioning the judgment store as a governed, provenance-bearing, LLM-era case base is a clean framing for the contribution and connects it to decades of prior work on when a precedent legitimately applies.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the classical foundation for case-grounded reuse and to structure the governed reuse loop on the R4 cycle.

sources.authors: Jeff Conklin, Michael L. Begeman
sources.title: gIBIS: A Hypertext Tool for Exploratory Policy Discussion
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS), 6(4), pp. 303-331
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM DL (10.1145/58566.59297), TOIS 6(4):303-331, 1988, plus dblp and a hosted PDF. Note a closely related CSCW '88 paper of the same title exists (DOI 10.1145/62266.62278) - cite the TOIS version for the journal record.
sources.what_it_establishes: A hypertext system implementing IBIS (Issue-Based Information Systems) to capture design deliberation as an explicit typed network of Issues, Positions and Arguments, aimed at preserving early design rationale on large complex problems.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The software-engineering ancestor of SQ2, and the source of its most important cautionary lesson. gIBIS attempted exactly what SQ2 attempts - make human deliberation and rationale into a structured, stored, reusable artefact - and the design rationale line of work that followed is well known for foundering on capture overhead: experts would not pay the cost of articulating rationale in a formal structure while doing their real work. That failure mode is the direct empirical link between SQ2 and SQ1: governed knowledge reuse is only viable if the capture burden is selective and low, which is precisely what SQ1's selective-intervention question is for. The thesis therefore gains a genuine novelty argument - agentic AI changes the economics of rationale capture, because the agent can draft the structured judgment record and the expert need only adjudicate it, inverting the gIBIS workload. Citing gIBIS also anchors the work in the software-modelling tradition that VEGO-AI belongs to, rather than only in ML.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the design-rationale precedent and its capture-overhead failure, then argue agentic drafting inverts that cost - linking SQ2 back to SQ1.

sources.authors: Rinke Hoekstra
sources.title: The Knowledge Reengineering Bottleneck
sources.venue: Semantic Web, 1(1-2), IOS Press
sources.verification_note: Author, title, journal (Semantic Web, IOS Press), year 2010 and DOI 10.3233/SW-2010-0004 confirmed via SAGE/IOS listing, the Semantic Web Journal site and ResearchGate. I could NOT confirm the exact page range from the sources I checked - obtain it from IOS Press before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: Argues that beyond Feigenbaum's classic knowledge ACQUISITION bottleneck there is a knowledge REENGINEERING bottleneck: ex ante 'think before you act' knowledge-engineering methodologies give no guidance for revising formalised knowledge after the fact, forcing ad hoc manual labour.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Sharpens the brittleness critique into exactly the form SQ2 needs. The commonplace point is that capturing expert knowledge is expensive; Hoekstra's point is the more damaging one for governance - that MAINTAINING and revising formalised knowledge as the domain shifts is the unsolved part, and that classical methodologies simply have no ex post story. SQ2's requirements for validation, reconciliation and controlled revision of stored judgment are a direct response to this, and citing Hoekstra lets the thesis say why a naive 'just build an expert knowledge base' approach - the obvious objection to SQ2 - has a known historical failure mode. It also pre-empts the criticism that a governed judgment store is a rebranded expert system: the difference is that SQ2 treats revision, scope limitation and retirement as first-class governed operations rather than as unplanned maintenance.
sources.citation_use: Cite in the gap analysis to distinguish acquisition from reengineering, and to justify why SQ2 designs for revision from the outset.

sources.authors: Margaret Mitchell, Simone Wu, Andrew Zaldivar, Parker Barnes, Lucy Vasserman, Ben Hutchinson, Elena Spitzer, Inioluwa Deborah Raji, Timnit Gebru
sources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
sources.venue: FAT* '19: Proceedings of the Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, Atlanta GA, pp. 220-229
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 1810.03993, dblp FAT* 2019 proceedings listing and multiple bibliographic records; DOI 10.1145/3287560.3287596 confirmed. Page range 220-229 is the commonly cited one but I did not confirm it directly - verify before final citation.
sources.what_it_establishes: A structured documentation framework requiring released models to be accompanied by declarations of intended use, out-of-scope use, evaluation conditions, and disaggregated performance characteristics.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the missing 'scope of valid reuse' vocabulary that PROV lacks and that SQ2 explicitly requires to prevent unsafe generalization. The model-card notion of intended and out-of-scope use, transposed from models to individual judgment records, is a concrete and already-legitimised mechanism: each stored expert ruling declares the modelling context, guideline version, and domain in which it was issued and may be reused, and everything beyond that is out of scope by default. That converts 'unsafe generalization' from a vague hazard into a checkable predicate at retrieval time, which is what makes SQ2's governance implementable and SQ3's transfer question answerable rather than rhetorical. Also relevant as accountability precedent - it is the FAccT community's established position that undocumented reuse of an artefact is itself a harm.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the precedent for declaring intended and out-of-scope use, and adapt it into per-judgment scope declarations governing retrieval.

sources.authors: Timnit Gebru, Jamie Morgenstern, Briana Vecchione, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan, Hanna Wallach, Hal Daume III, Kate Crawford
sources.title: Datasheets for Datasets
sources.venue: Communications of the ACM, 64(12), pp. 86-92
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM DL / CACM (10.1145/3458723), CACM Dec 2021 vol. 64 no. 12 pp. 86-92, and arXiv 1803.09010 for the earlier version. Authors, venue and pagination match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Proposes that every dataset ship with a datasheet documenting motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing, recommended uses and maintenance, to standardise communication between dataset creators and consumers - with explicit emphasis on high-stakes domains.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The companion documentation precedent to model cards, operating at the level of the knowledge artefact rather than the model, which is where SQ2's judgment store sits. Two elements are directly transferable: the COLLECTION PROCESS section, which for a judgment store means recording who the expert was, what they were asked, what context they saw and under what elicitation protocol - metadata without which a stored ruling cannot be validated or contested later; and the MAINTENANCE section, which asks who is responsible for updating the artefact and how consumers are notified of changes, which is the governance-ownership question SQ2 must answer for a judgment store that persists across guideline revisions. The high-stakes framing also strengthens the SQ3 healthcare argument that documentation obligations increase, not decrease, when knowledge crosses into clinical contexts.
sources.citation_use: Cite for the elicitation-context and maintenance-responsibility metadata that a governed judgment record must carry.

sources.authors: Hannah Rashkin, Vitaly Nikolaev, Matthew Lamm, Lora Aroyo, Michael Collins, Dipanjan Das, Slav Petrov, Gaurav Singh Tomar, Iulia Turc, David Reitter
sources.title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models
sources.venue: Computational Linguistics, 49(4), pp. 777-840
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via MIT Press Direct (10.1162/coli_a_00486), ACL Anthology (2023.cl-4.2), Google Research publications page and DOAJ. Volume 49, issue 4, pp. 777-840, 2023 - all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: The AIS (Attributable to Identified Sources) evaluation framework, which defines when generated text is genuinely supported by a provided source, plus a two-stage human annotation pipeline for applying that judgment reliably.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Provides the measurement instrument for the 'transparently' clause in SQ2 - reuse must be not only traceable in principle but demonstrably grounded in fact. Storing expert judgment with provenance is worthless if the agent's output does not actually follow from the retrieved rulings, and AIS is the established, peer-reviewed way to test that: is this variability assessment attributable to the identified expert judgment records it cites, or is the citation decorative? That turns a governance claim into an empirical evaluation the thesis can run. The two-stage annotation pipeline is directly reusable as protocol for the human evaluation. Note that Lora Aroyo is a co-author here and on the crowd-truth paper, giving the thesis a coherent line from 'disagreement is signal' through to 'attribution is measurable'.
sources.citation_use: Cite as the evaluation instrument for whether agent outputs are genuinely attributable to the stored judgment records they cite.

sources.authors: Mor Peleg
sources.title: Computer-interpretable Clinical Guidelines: A Methodological Review
sources.venue: Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 46(4), pp. 744-763
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ScienceDirect (S1532046413000841), PubMed 23806274 and Semantic Scholar. JBI 46(4):744-763, Aug 2013, sole author Mor Peleg, University of Haifa Department of Information Systems - all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: Comprehensive methodological review of formalising narrative clinical practice guidelines into computer-interpretable guidelines (CIGs), covering modelling languages, the acquisition and formalisation process, verification, exception handling and known adoption barriers.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The bridge source connecting SQ2 to SQ3 and to the thesis's own vocabulary, since 'guideline operationalization' is the umbrella term and this is the definitive review of what that has meant in the highest-stakes domain. It documents a mature discipline that has already confronted SQ2's exact problems - formalising expert consensus, handling the gap between a guideline's general statement and a specific patient's circumstances, versioning knowledge as guidelines are revised, and the persistent difficulty that formalisation requires scarce expert time. That gives SQ3 a concrete, well-studied target context for transfer rather than a speculative one, and lets the thesis argue continuity: variability in student UML models against a modelling guideline and variability in clinical practice against a care guideline are instances of one problem class. Strategically notable that Peleg is at the University of Haifa Information Systems department, the same institutional setting as the VEGO-AI work, which makes this a realistic collaboration path for the healthcare arm subject to the governance constraints SQ3 names.
sources.citation_use: Cite to define guideline operationalization in the clinical setting and to justify healthcare as SQ3's transfer target with a documented prior literature.

sources.authors: Kars Alfrink, Ianus Keller, Gerd Kortuem, Neelke Doorn
sources.title: Contestable AI by Design: Towards a Framework
sources.venue: Minds and Machines, 33(4), pp. 613-639
sources.verification_note: Paper, authors, journal, volume 33 issue 4 and pages 613-639 confirmed via the TU Delft Research Portal, PhilPapers and the DOI. YEAR IS AMBIGUOUS: the DOI suffix and online-first publication are 2022 while the journal issue is 2023, and different databases report each. Confirm which year your citation style requires.
sources.what_it_establishes: Synthesises from the literature a design framework for contestable AI - systems built to remain responsive to human intervention throughout their lifecycle, with mechanisms for challenging and revising automated decisions rather than only explaining them.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the normative backbone for SQ2's clause about reuse 'without loss of human authority', which is otherwise the softest and least operationalised part of the question. Contestability is a stronger and more precise requirement than explainability: it demands not just that a stored expert ruling be visible, but that there be a working mechanism by which a human can challenge it, trigger review, and have it overturned or scoped - which is exactly what distinguishes a governed judgment store from a static knowledge base. The framework's lifecycle emphasis also matters, because SQ2's risk is not only at capture but at every later reuse where a precedent is applied to a case its author never considered. Gives the thesis design requirements it can be evaluated against, and connects the technical contribution to accountability and legitimacy arguments that a doctoral committee outside ML will expect to see engaged.
sources.citation_use: Cite to operationalise 'human authority' as contestability requirements on the judgment store, and to derive evaluable design criteria.

sources.authors: Sinno Jialin Pan, Qiang Yang
sources.title: A Survey on Transfer Learning
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering, 22(10), 1345-1359
sources.verification_note: Title, authors, year, journal, volume/issue and page range all confirmed across multiple independent records (SCIRP reference entries, BibSonomy, hosted PDF at cubs.buffalo.edu). DOI 10.1109/TKDE.2009.191 confirmed.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical taxonomy of transfer learning: it separates transductive transfer (same task, different domain - i.e. domain adaptation), inductive transfer (different task), and unsupervised transfer, and it explicitly names 'negative transfer' as the failure mode where source knowledge degrades target performance.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 its primary CLASSIFICATION AXIS. The thesis needs a principled vocabulary for what kind of transfer it is claiming when captured expert judgment moves from student UML models to another guideline-operationalization context. Under Pan & Yang's scheme, moving VEGO-AI judgment from software modelling to a second modelling corpus is transductive transfer (task fixed - substantial vs occasional - domain changes), whereas moving it to healthcare is inductive transfer (the task itself changes). Forcing the thesis to state which case it is prevents the vague 'it generalizes' claim. 'Negative transfer' is the name for exactly the risk SQ3 calls unsafe generalization, so this paper supplies the term of art the thesis should adopt.

sources.authors: Fuzhen Zhuang, Zhiyuan Qi, Keyu Duan, Dongbo Xi, Yongchun Zhu, Hengshu Zhu, Hui Xiong, Qing He
sources.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Transfer Learning
sources.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE, 109(1), 43-76
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Rutgers institutional repository, publisher-hosted PDF at datamining.rutgers.edu, and arXiv preprint 1911.02685. Volume 109, issue 1, pages 43-76, January 2021, DOI 10.1109/JPROC.2020.3004555 all match.
sources.what_it_establishes: An updated and much broader survey than Pan & Yang, organizing ~forty representative transfer methods into two mechanism families: data-based interpretation (reweighting and feature transformation of instances) and model-based interpretation (parameter sharing, control, and model ensembling).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 a MECHANISM MENU for the specific question 'what is actually being transferred?'. Because the thesis transfers captured human judgment rather than model weights, the data-based/model-based split is directly usable as a design contrast: judgment stored as reusable exemplar cases is a data-based transfer, whereas judgment baked into agent prompts, rubrics, or a policy is model-based. Naming this distinction lets the thesis argue why a case-based, human-auditable representation is more governable under transfer than a parameterized one - which is the bridge from SQ2 (representation) to SQ3 (transfer).

sources.authors: Karl Weiss, Taghi M. Khoshgoftaar, DingDing Wang
sources.title: A survey of transfer learning
sources.venue: Journal of Big Data, 3, Article 9
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Springer (open access), DBLP record journals/jbd/WeissK016, and multiple citation databases. Journal of Big Data volume 3 (2016), DOI 10.1186/s40537-016-0043-6. Commonly cited with page range 1-40.
sources.what_it_establishes: Formalizes the homogeneous vs heterogeneous transfer distinction (same feature space vs different feature space) and devotes explicit treatment to negative transfer detection and to how solutions differ when the source and target do not even share a representation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Directly frames the hardest version of SQ3. Moving judgment from UML domain models to healthcare guideline operationalization is HETEROGENEOUS transfer - the artifacts, the feature space, and the expert population all change - which is a far stronger claim than the homogeneous case. This survey gives the thesis the argument for why the healthcare arm must be treated as a separate, more demanding validation regime rather than 'more of the same evaluation', and supplies negative-transfer detection as a concrete safety check the governance layer can require before reuse is permitted.

sources.authors: Joaquin Quiñonero-Candela, Masashi Sugiyama, Anton Schwaighofer, Neil D. Lawrence (eds.)
sources.title: Dataset Shift in Machine Learning
sources.venue: MIT Press (Neural Information Processing series)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via MIT Press Books Gateway, Crossref DOI chooser (10.7551/mitpress/9780262170055.001.0001), a review in the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A (173(1), 274), and the University of Edinburgh research explorer. ISBN 9780262170055.
sources.what_it_establishes: The reference taxonomy of dataset shift: covariate shift (P(x) changes, P(y|x) stable), prior probability shift (P(y) changes), and concept shift (P(y|x) itself changes) - i.e. the decision rule, not just the inputs, has moved.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the single most diagnostically useful axis for SQ3 and the thesis should build its transfer test matrix on it. If a new corpus of domain models merely contains different modelling topics, that is covariate shift and stored judgment may safely transfer. If a new expert community draws the substantial/occasional line differently, that is CONCEPT SHIFT and reusing stored judgment is unsafe by construction. Separating these two cases empirically is precisely what 'testing honestly' means for SQ3, and it converts the vague governance rule 'do not over-generalize' into a measurable condition.

sources.authors: João Gama, Indrė Žliobaitė, Albert Bifet, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Abdelhamid Bouchachia
sources.title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
sources.venue: ACM Computing Surveys, 46(4), Article 44
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/2523813), and institutional repositories at TU Eindhoven, Helsinki, Aalto, Bournemouth and IP Paris. ACM Computing Surveys volume 46, issue 4, 2014.
sources.what_it_establishes: A full treatment of concept drift - change in the target concept over time - covering drift types (sudden, gradual, incremental, recurring), drift detection methods, adaptation strategies, and crucially the EVALUATION methodology for adaptive learners (prequential / test-then-train error rather than a static held-out split).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies the TEMPORAL dimension of SQ3, which is otherwise easy to miss. Transfer is not only across sites and domains but across time: an expert judgment captured in 2026 about what counts as substantial variability may quietly stop holding as modelling conventions, curricula, or the underlying LLM agents change. This gives the thesis (a) the vocabulary for recurring vs gradual drift in a judgment repository, and (b) a concrete evaluation protocol - prequential evaluation - suited to a knowledge store that is continuously appended to, which a single train/test split cannot honestly assess.

sources.authors: Pang Wei Koh, Shiori Sagawa, Henrik Marklund, Sang Michael Xie, Marvin Zhang, Akshay Balsubramani, Weihua Hu, Michihiro Yasunaga, Richard Lanas Phillips, Irena Gao, Tony Lee, Etienne David, Ian Stavness, Wei Guo, Berton Earnshaw, Imran Haque, Sara Beery, Jure Leskovec, Anshul Kundaje, Emma Pierson, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn, Percy Liang
sources.title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 139
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the official ICML 2021 virtual site (oral presentation), Stanford-hosted camera-ready PDF (wilds-icml21.pdf), and Semantic Scholar. Full 23-author list confirmed. Note an earlier arXiv version circulated in 2020, so some databases show 2020 for the preprint.
sources.what_it_establishes: A curated benchmark of real, naturally-occurring distribution shifts, built around two distinct shift types: DOMAIN GENERALIZATION (test domains unseen at training time, e.g. new hospitals, new countries, new codebases) and SUBPOPULATION SHIFT (all groups seen, but their proportions change). It documents large in-distribution vs out-of-distribution performance gaps that standard training does not close.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 its core EVALUATION DESIGN PATTERN and its headline metric. The WILDS convention of always reporting an in-distribution number alongside an out-of-distribution number, with the gap as the quantity of interest, is exactly the honest reporting protocol the thesis should adopt for reused judgment: performance on the corpus that produced the judgment versus performance on a held-out corpus. WILDS also legitimizes structuring evaluation splits by real grouping variables (institution, cohort, project) rather than random splits - which for this thesis means splitting by student cohort, course, or modelling task, not by individual model.

sources.authors: Ishaan Gulrajani, David Lopez-Paz
sources.title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
sources.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the official ICLR 2021 poster page (iclr.cc/virtual/2021/poster/2998) and the SlidesLive recording listing both authors. The DomainBed testbed (7 benchmarks, 14 algorithms, 3 model selection criteria) and the ERM-is-competitive finding are confirmed in those records.
sources.what_it_establishes: That apparent progress in domain generalization largely dissolves under a controlled protocol: with equal tuning budgets and an explicitly stated model selection criterion, plain empirical risk minimization matches state-of-the-art. The central methodological point is that MODEL SELECTION IS PART OF THE PROBLEM - if you tune on the target domain you have already leaked, and results are not comparable unless the selection rule is declared.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the strongest available warning against a specific way SQ3 could go wrong. If the thesis tunes its intervention thresholds, reuse rules, or agent prompts while looking at the transfer corpus, any transfer result is an artifact. Gulrajani & Lopez-Paz give the thesis (a) a requirement to pre-declare the model/threshold selection rule before touching the transfer set, and (b) a strong, honest BASELINE discipline: the governed-reuse mechanism must be shown to beat the naive baseline of simply re-running VEGO-AI with no stored judgment at all, under identical budgets. Without that baseline the contribution is unfalsifiable.

sources.authors: Benjamin Recht, Rebecca Roelofs, Ludwig Schmidt, Vaishaal Shankar
sources.title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 97
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via PMLR proceedings v97, DBLP record conf/icml/RechtRSS19, the ICML 2019 oral listing, and researchr. All four authors, title and year match.
sources.what_it_establishes: That building genuinely new test sets, following the original collection protocol as closely as possible, still produced accuracy drops of roughly 10% across many models - and that the drop was attributable to models failing on slightly harder in-distribution examples rather than to adaptive overfitting from test-set reuse.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 a decisive methodological move and a calibration expectation. The move: to test whether captured judgment holds, COLLECT A FRESH EVALUATION SET under the same protocol rather than re-splitting the original corpus. The calibration: expect a real drop even when nothing about the setting has formally changed, so the thesis must define in advance what size of drop counts as acceptable transfer versus a governance stop. This also protects the thesis from the reviewer objection that a modest performance decline invalidates the approach - Recht et al. establish that some decline is the norm even under best-effort replication.

sources.authors: Shachar Kaufman, Saharon Rosset, Claudia Perlich, Ori Stitelman
sources.title: Leakage in data mining: Formulation, detection, and avoidance
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data (TKDD), 6(4), Article 15
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/2382577.2382579), researchr record KaufmanRPS12, Tel Aviv University and IUCC repositories. TKDD 6(4):15, 2012; an earlier version appeared at KDD 2011. Fourth author Ori Stitelman is often omitted in short citations.
