sources.what_it_establishes: The first rigorous formulation of leakage as the introduction of information about the target that would not legitimately be available at prediction time, plus two operational contributions: the 'learn-predict separation' principle for avoiding it by construction, and detection techniques for when the modeller did not control data collection.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 its primary LEAKAGE CONTROL, and the thesis has an acute leakage risk that this paper names precisely. A repository of stored expert judgment is a channel through which target-side information can flow into the assessment of a new case: if judgment captured about model M is reused when scoring M itself, or when scoring a near-duplicate from the same student cohort, the reuse mechanism will look effective for the wrong reason. Learn-predict separation translates into a hard architectural rule for the governance layer - the retrieval index must be partitioned so that no judgment originating from the evaluation partition can ever be retrieved during evaluation. That rule is a designable, checkable artifact, not just a caveat.

sources.authors: Sayash Kapoor, Arvind Narayanan
sources.title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
sources.venue: Patterns, 4(9), Article 100804
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Cell Press/Patterns full text, PubMed 37720327, NSF PAGES record, and institutional repositories. Patterns volume 4, issue 9, article 100804, 1 September 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100804. Open access.
sources.what_it_establishes: A survey finding leakage across 17 scientific fields affecting 294 papers, an eight-type taxonomy of leakage running from textbook errors (no clean train/test split) through subtler forms (illegitimate features, temporal leakage, non-independence between train and test samples, sampling bias in the test distribution), and 'model info sheets' as a reporting instrument for pre-empting leakage claims.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The single most directly actionable methodology source for SQ3. Three of the eight leakage types map onto concrete hazards in this thesis: non-independence between train and test (multiple UML models from the same student, team, or assignment must not straddle the split), temporal leakage (judgment captured later must not inform earlier cases), and sampling bias in the test set (a transfer corpus that quietly resembles the source proves nothing). The MODEL INFO SHEET is also a ready-made governance artifact - it is a leakage-disclosure template the thesis can adapt into the reuse-audit record required by SQ2, which makes it a rare source that serves SQ2 and SQ3 simultaneously.

sources.authors: Oscar Sainz, Jon Ander Campos, Iker García-Ferrero, Julen Etxaniz, Oier Lopez de Lacalle, Eneko Agirre
sources.title: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
sources.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023, pages 10776-10787
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACL Anthology (2023.findings-emnlp.722), DBLP record conf/emnlp/SainzCGELA23, and the associated LM Contamination Index repository (hitz-zentroa/lm-contamination). All six authors and page range confirmed.
sources.what_it_establishes: A position argument that benchmark-based evaluation of LLMs is no longer sound unless contamination is measured per benchmark, since the worst case - the model was trained on the benchmark's test split - is indistinguishable from genuine capability at the score level. It also motivates community-level contamination registries.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Names a validity threat unique to an LLM-agent thesis and therefore unavoidable for SQ3. VEGO-AI's agents are LLMs; if the domain models, guidelines, or textbook UML exercises used for evaluation were in pretraining data, then apparent transfer of judgment may just be memorization surfacing. This source obliges the thesis to (a) state contamination risk explicitly as a threat to validity, and (b) prefer freshly authored or access-restricted student artifacts for the transfer arm. It is also the clearest justification for why the healthcare arm - if governance permits - should use data that provably could not have been in a public crawl.

sources.authors: Shahriar Golchin, Mihai Surdeanu
sources.title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
sources.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the official ICLR 2024 poster page (iclr.cc/virtual/2024/poster/19550), the ICLR proceedings hash page, OpenReview forum 2Rwq6c3tvr, and arXiv 2308.08493. Both authors confirmed.
sources.what_it_establishes: An operational method for DETECTING contamination without access to the pretraining corpus: 'guided instruction' prompts the model with the dataset name, partition, and a truncated reference instance and measures how well it completes it, first at instance level and then aggregated to partition level.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Turns the contamination threat from an unaddressable caveat into a MEASURABLE CHECK that the thesis can actually run. Because Golchin & Surdeanu's method needs only black-box access, it works against the commercial LLMs a VEGO-AI-style system uses. For SQ3 this means the transfer evaluation can include a pre-registered contamination probe on each corpus before any transfer claim is made, and can report a contamination estimate alongside the in-distribution/out-of-distribution gap. That is a concrete, defensible answer to the examiner question 'how do you know the agents were not just recalling these models?'.

sources.authors: June Sallou, Thomas Durieux, Annibale Panichella
sources.title: Breaking the Silence: the Threats of Using LLMs in Software Engineering
sources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 46th International Conference on Software Engineering: New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/3639476.3639764), TU Delft research portal, the ICSE 2024 NIER programme page, DBLP conf/icse/nier2024, and arXiv 2312.08055. Note: some records label it the 44th ICSE and others the 46th; ICSE 2024 Lisbon is the 46th, so the '44th' label in one ACM listing appears to be a metadata error rather than a different paper.
sources.what_it_establishes: A structured catalogue of threats to validity specific to LLM-based software engineering research - closed-source and non-versioned models, non-determinism, data leakage between LLM pretraining data and SE evaluation benchmarks, and irreproducibility of findings - together with mitigation guidelines addressed both to SE researchers and to model providers.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the VALIDITY THREAT FRAMEWORK written for exactly this thesis's setting: LLM agents evaluated on software engineering artifacts. It gives SQ3 a domain-appropriate checklist to structure its threats-to-validity section, rather than importing a generic ML one. It is also the natural place to anchor a reproducibility commitment - pinning model versions, logging temperature and seeds, archiving prompts - which matters more here than usual, because if the underlying agents silently change, a later attempt to reuse stored judgment is testing a different system, and the transfer result cannot be interpreted.

sources.authors: Claes Wohlin, Per Runeson, Martin Höst, Magnus C. Ohlsson, Björn Regnell, Anders Wesslén
sources.title: Experimentation in Software Engineering
sources.venue: Springer-Verlag, Berlin Heidelberg
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Springer Nature Link (DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2), Lund University research portal, and Google Books. ISBN 9783642290435. Note there is an earlier 2000 Kluwer edition titled 'Experimentation in Software Engineering: An Introduction' (DOI 10.1007/978-1-4615-4625-2) - cite the 2012 edition to avoid ambiguity.
sources.what_it_establishes: The standard SE adaptation of the Cook & Campbell validity scheme - conclusion, internal, construct and external validity - with named threat sub-categories, plus full protocols for the five experiment stages (scoping, planning, operation, analysis, presentation) including the treatment of student subjects.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The methodological BACKBONE for SQ3's evaluation chapter, and unusually well matched because the VEGO-AI corpus is student-produced - a setting this book treats explicitly rather than dismissing. Two of its external-validity threat categories are the thesis's real risks under their standard names: 'interaction of selection and treatment' (judgment captured from one expert population may not hold for another) and 'interaction of setting and treatment' (a university modelling exercise is not an industrial or clinical setting). Using this shared vocabulary means SE examiners will read the transfer limitations as rigour rather than as weakness.

sources.authors: Janet Siegmund, Norbert Siegmund, Sven Apel
sources.title: Views on Internal and External Validity in Empirical Software Engineering
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE), Volume 1, pages 9-19
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM Digital Library, Semantic Scholar, and Sven Apel's publication list at Saarland University (se.cs.uni-saarland.de), which records ICSE 2015, pages 9-19, and an ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Award. A retrospective '10 years validity' PDF is hosted at Universität Leipzig.
sources.what_it_establishes: Survey evidence from the SE research community showing there is NO consensus on the internal/external validity trade-off, on when each should be prioritized, or on how replications should be conducted and reviewed - and that reviewers apply these criteria inconsistently.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Serves two purposes for SQ3. Substantively, it is the empirical warrant for treating external validity as a first-class research question rather than a closing caveat - which is precisely the framing move this thesis needs to justify SQ3 existing at all. Defensively, it pre-empts the reviewer who insists there is one correct way to trade internal against external validity: Siegmund et al. show the community itself disagrees, so the thesis's obligation is to declare and justify its position, not to satisfy an imagined consensus. It also directly motivates the replication design that SQ3's transfer arm amounts to.

sources.authors: Rogardt Heldal
sources.title: Is generalisation hindering the adoption of your findings?
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 18th ACM/IEEE International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM), pages 348-358
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/3674805.3686694) and OpenAlex, which both list Rogardt Heldal (Western Norway University of Applied Sciences) as the SOLE author. Published 15 October 2024, pages 348-358. Worth noting the single-author attribution, since the topic might suggest a larger team.
sources.what_it_establishes: A reflective account of a failed attempt to build a general artifact for managing software product variability across five organizations. The retrospective concludes that the pursuit of generalisation itself produced a solution too abstract to be useful to any of the organizations, and that none were willing to invest in concretizing it.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: An unusually well-targeted CONTRAST CASE - it is about variability management, the same problem family as VEGO-AI, and it argues the opposite of the default assumption behind SQ3. Where most transfer literature treats broader generalization as the goal, Heldal shows over-generalisation as the failure mode: judgment abstracted enough to transfer everywhere may carry too little content to be actionable anywhere. This gives SQ3 a genuine research tension to resolve rather than a foregone conclusion, and it argues for evaluating transferred judgment on USEFULNESS and adoption in the target context, not only on agreement scores. It is also the sharpest justification for the thesis's 'without unsafe generalization' qualifier.

sources.authors: Thomas Zimmermann, Nachiappan Nagappan, Harald Gall, Emanuel Giger, Brendan Murphy
sources.title: Cross-project defect prediction: a large scale experiment on data vs. domain vs. process
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 7th Joint Meeting of the European Software Engineering Conference and the ACM SIGSOFT Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE), pages 91-100
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Semantic Scholar, University of Zurich ZORA repository, and multiple citing papers. ESEC/FSE 2009, pages 91-100, DOI 10.1145/1595696.1595713. The 622 cross-project prediction runs across 12 real-world applications is confirmed in the abstract.
sources.what_it_establishes: The landmark negative result on transfer within software engineering: across 622 cross-project prediction experiments, only a small fraction succeeded, and success was not predictable from surface similarity - it depended jointly on data characteristics, domain, and development process. The paper then builds a model to predict in advance WHETHER a given transfer will work.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most important SE-native precedent for SQ3, and it supplies both a sobering baseline and a design idea. The baseline: in software engineering, naive transfer of a learned artifact between projects usually FAILS, so the thesis should expect and plan for failure cases rather than presenting transfer as the default. The design idea is the more valuable one - Zimmermann et al. do not merely measure transfer, they learn a decision procedure for when transfer is advisable. That is structurally what SQ3 needs the governance layer to do: not a blanket permit-or-forbid rule for reusing stored judgment, but a context-similarity gate that decides per case, which also feeds back into SQ1's selective-intervention logic (a refused transfer is exactly the moment to escalate to a human).

sources.authors: Ewout W. Steyerberg, Frank E. Harrell Jr.
sources.title: Prediction models need appropriate internal, internal-external, and external validation
sources.venue: Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 69, 245-247
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, PubMed 25981519, and the Erasmus University Rotterdam repository. Volume 69, pages 245-247, DOI 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2015.04.005. Published online 2015, issue year 2016 - both years appear in citation databases.
sources.what_it_establishes: A three-level validation hierarchy: internal validation (bootstrap/cross-validation, addressing reproducibility within the development sample), INTERNAL-EXTERNAL validation (leave-one-cluster-out across the natural groupings already present in the data, e.g. centres or studies), and fully external validation (a genuinely independent sample). It also argues against wasteful random data splitting.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives SQ3 the crucial MIDDLE RUNG, which is what makes the research question tractable within a PhD. The thesis is unlikely to obtain a fully independent healthcare corpus early, and pure internal validation proves nothing about transfer. Internal-external validation - leave-one-cohort-out or leave-one-course-out over the existing VEGO-AI corpus - yields a defensible transfer claim from data already in hand, and it generalizes cleanly to leave-one-expert-out, which tests whether captured judgment holds beyond the individual who produced it. That is arguably the single most important empirical test SQ3 can run, and this paper is its methodological citation.

sources.authors: Chava L. Ramspek, Kitty J. Jager, Friedo W. Dekker, Carmine Zoccali, Merel van Diepen
sources.title: External validation of prognostic models: what, why, how, when and where?
sources.venue: Clinical Kidney Journal, 14(1), 49-58
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Oxford Academic, PubMed 33564405, PMC7857818, Amsterdam UMC and Leiden University repositories. Clinical Kidney Journal volume 14, issue 1, January 2021, pages 49-58, DOI 10.1093/ckj/sfaa188. Open access.
sources.what_it_establishes: A practical how-to for external validation: the distinction between REPRODUCIBILITY (does it hold in similar patients from the same underlying population?) and TRANSPORTABILITY (does it hold in a plausibly related but different population?); the taxonomy of validation designs (temporal, geographical, domain); and the insistence on reporting calibration as well as discrimination. It also documents that external validation is rarely done, and almost never by independent investigators.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Supplies SQ3's most precise conceptual distinction and a metric the thesis is at risk of omitting. Reproducibility vs transportability lets the thesis state exactly which claim it is making for each transfer arm - a second modelling corpus is a transportability test, a later cohort of the same course is a reproducibility test - and stops the two being conflated. The temporal/geographical/domain design taxonomy maps directly onto later cohorts, other institutions, and healthcare respectively, giving a ready-made three-arm evaluation structure. Most importantly, the emphasis on CALIBRATION over raw discrimination matters here: an agentic system that still ranks cases correctly in a new context but is systematically overconfident about when it needs no human input is a governance failure that accuracy metrics alone would hide.

sources.authors: Gary S. Collins, Karel G. M. Moons, Paula Dhiman, Richard D. Riley, Andrew L. Beam, Ben Van Calster, Marzyeh Ghassemi, Xiaoxuan Liu, et al.
sources.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
sources.verification_note: Fully verified by fetching the PubMed record (PMID 38626948): title, author order, journal BMJ, volume 385, article e078378, year 2024, DOI 10.1136/bmj-2023-078378 all confirmed. Supersedes the original 2015 TRIPOD statement; the checklist has 27 items. Also confirmed via PMC11025451 and Oxford/Birmingham/UCL/Maastricht repositories.
sources.what_it_establishes: The current consensus reporting standard for prediction models built with either regression or machine learning: a 27-item checklist covering data sources and participant selection, handling of predictors, model development, evaluation of performance including calibration, fairness considerations, and - critically - explicit reporting of whether a study is development, validation, or both, and in what population.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The REPORTING INSTRUMENT for SQ3's healthcare arm, and a governance artifact in its own right. If the thesis ever touches clinical guideline operationalization, TRIPOD+AI is what reviewers and ethics committees will expect, so adopting it early shapes what must be recorded from the outset rather than reconstructed later. Beyond compliance, its structure is directly transplantable to the software side: the requirement to state the intended population and use context for a model is the analogue of the scope-of-validity metadata that SQ2's judgment repository must attach to each stored judgment, and that SQ3 must then test. It is the clearest existing evidence that mature fields govern transfer through mandatory disclosure of context, which is the mechanism this thesis is proposing.

sources.authors: John R. Zech, Marcus A. Badgeley, Manway Liu, Anthony B. Costa, Joseph J. Titano, Eric Karl Oermann
sources.title: Variable generalization performance of a deep learning model to detect pneumonia in chest radiographs: A cross-sectional study
sources.venue: PLoS Medicine, 15(11), e1002683
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via PLoS Medicine, PubMed 30399157, and the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai research portal. Volume 15, issue 11, article e1002683, November 2018, DOI 10.1371/journal.pmed.1002683. All six authors confirmed.
sources.what_it_establishes: A controlled cross-institution generalization study across three hospital systems showing that performance degrades substantially on external sites, and - the deeper finding - that the model had learned to infer the hospital system from image artifacts and exploit site-specific disease prevalence as a shortcut. Internal performance was therefore inflated by a confounder invisible to standard evaluation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The canonical demonstration that INTERNAL PERFORMANCE CAN BE A LIE, and the mechanism it identifies is live in this thesis. VEGO-AI's agents could just as easily learn cohort- or assignment-specific surface cues - a course's modelling conventions, a template, a recurring diagram style - and appear to distinguish substantial from occasional variability while actually keying on provenance. Zech et al. give SQ3 a specific diagnostic obligation: run a site/cohort-identification probe to check whether the system can recover the origin of an artifact it should be blind to, since a system that can is a system whose apparent judgment quality is partly confounded. This is a concrete experiment, not a caveat, and it is exactly the kind of honest test SQ3 is asking for.

sources.authors: Andrew Wong, Erkin Otles, John P. Donnelly, Andrew Krumm, Jeffrey McCullough, Olivia DeTroyer-Cooley, Justin Pestrue, Marie Phillips, Judy Konye, Carleen Penoza, Muhammad Ghous, Karandeep Singh
sources.title: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
sources.venue: JAMA Internal Medicine, 181(8), 1065-1070
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via JAMA Network, PubMed 34152373, and Semantic Scholar. JAMA Internal Medicine volume 181, issue 8, pages 1065-1070, published online 21 June 2021, DOI 10.1001/jamainternmed.2021.2626. Lead authors Wong, Otles, Donnelly, Krumm, McCullough (University of Michigan) confirmed; the full author list is long and some records truncate it.
sources.what_it_establishes: An independent external validation of the Epic Sepsis Model - deployed at hundreds of hospitals - finding substantially worse discrimination than the vendor claimed, poor calibration, missed cases, and a high alert burden. A widely trusted, widely deployed model failed its first rigorous outside test.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The strongest available MOTIVATING CASE for why SQ3 must exist as a research question rather than a validation step, and it is doubly on-point because the failure was partly about ALERT BURDEN - the same quantity SQ1 is trying to manage. Wong et al. show a system that both under-detected and over-alerted, which is precisely the twin failure mode a selective-intervention policy risks when its thresholds are carried into a new context unchanged. For the thesis this argues that transferred judgment must be re-validated on intervention volume and precision at the new site, not only on agreement with experts, and it supplies a real-world illustration that vendor or developer self-evaluation is not a substitute for independent external validation.

sources.authors: Joseph Futoma, Morgan Simons, Trishan Panch, Finale Doshi-Velez, Leo Anthony Celi
sources.title: The myth of generalisability in clinical research and machine learning in health care
sources.venue: The Lancet Digital Health, 2(9), e489-e492
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via The Lancet Digital Health (PII S2589-7500(20)30186-2), PubMed 32864600, Semantic Scholar, and Finale Doshi-Velez's Harvard publication page. Volume 2, issue 9, pages e489-e492, 2020. All five authors confirmed.
sources.what_it_establishes: A direct challenge to generalisability as the default goal: the authors argue that demanding broad generalisability can destroy clinical utility, and that narrowly-scoped, locally validated, continuously updated models may serve patients better than a single model claimed to work everywhere.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Reframes SQ3's success criterion, and pairs with Heldal 2024 to form the thesis's counter-position. Read together, the SE paper and the clinical paper make the same argument from opposite fields: the right question is not 'does the captured judgment generalize?' but 'over what scope is it valid, and what is the cheapest honest way to re-establish validity locally?'. That reframing is what lets SQ3 be about GOVERNED reuse rather than maximal reuse - the contribution becomes a mechanism for scoping and re-validating judgment, with local recalibration as a first-class outcome rather than an admission of failure. It also supplies the strongest argument for why 'unsafe generalization' is the risk to design against, and it is a citable authority for declining to over-claim on the healthcare arm.

sources.authors: Barbara Plank
sources.title: The 'Problem' of Human Label Variation: On Ground Truth in Data, Modeling and Evaluation
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), Abu Dhabi
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via arXiv 2211.02570, Semantic Scholar, and the accompanying EMNLP 2022 resource repository (mainlp/awesome-human-label-variation). Single author, EMNLP 2022 main conference. Page numbers were not independently confirmed in this session, so cite via the ACL Anthology entry to be safe.
sources.what_it_establishes: That disagreement among annotators is frequently GENUINE signal - arising from subjectivity, legitimate multiple readings, or ambiguity - rather than noise to be aggregated away, and that treating a single aggregated label as ground truth distorts every downstream stage: data, modeling, and evaluation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Resolves a confound that would otherwise make SQ3's central measurement uninterpretable, and it is the piece most literature on transfer misses. When judgment captured from expert A is reused in a new context and disagrees with expert B, there are two very different explanations: the judgment failed to transfer, or both experts are legitimately right and the substantial/occasional boundary is genuinely plural at that point. Plank's framing forces SQ3's design to separate these - for example by collecting unaggregated multi-expert labels on the transfer set so that irreducible human variation can be estimated and used as the CEILING against which transfer performance is judged. Without that ceiling the thesis cannot say whether a transfer result is bad or simply at the limit of what agreement can be. It also connects SQ3 back to SQ2, since a repository that stores only aggregated verdicts destroys the very information needed to test transfer honestly.

sources.authors: Alan R. Hevner, Salvatore T. March, Jinsoo Park, Sudha Ram
sources.title: Design Science in Information Systems Research
sources.venue: MIS Quarterly, Vol. 28, No. 1, pp. 75-106
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref API (DOI 10.2307/25148625): title, all four authors, MIS Quarterly, vol 28, iss 1, pp 75-106, 2004. Cross-checked against AIS eLibrary record aisel.aisnet.org/misq/vol28/iss1/6/ and the MISQ publisher page misq.umn.edu/misq/article/28/1/75/261 (article starts p.75). Note: MISQ articles of this era have no publisher DOI; 10.2307/25148625 is the JSTOR DOI and is the one indexed by Crossref.
sources.what_it_establishes: The canonical statement of design science as a legitimate IS research paradigm alongside behavioural science. Establishes the environment / IS-research / knowledge-base framework, the four artifact types inherited from March & Smith (constructs, models, methods, instantiations), and the seven guidelines (design as an artifact; problem relevance; design evaluation; research contributions; research rigor; design as a search process; communication of research).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the paper that lets the thesis claim its governed-judgment layer is a research artifact rather than engineering work bolted onto VEGO-AI. Concretely: the SQ1 selective-intervention policy is a *method* artifact, the judgment repository in SQ2 is a *model + method* artifact, and the extension of the VEGO-AI four-agent pipeline is the *instantiation*. Guideline 3 (design evaluation) and Guideline 5 (research rigor) are the two the evaluation chapter must be seen to satisfy. The environment/knowledge-base split also maps cleanly onto this project: environment = modelling instructors and domain experts producing the UML domain models VEGO-AI classifies as substantial vs occasional; knowledge base = the variability/SPL and human-in-the-loop uncertainty literatures. Cite as the foundational anchor of the methodology chapter.

sources.authors: Ken Peffers, Tuure Tuunanen, Marcus A. Rothenberger, Samir Chatterjee
sources.title: A Design Science Research Methodology for Information Systems Research
sources.venue: Journal of Management Information Systems, Vol. 24, No. 3, pp. 45-77
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref API (DOI 10.2753/MIS0742-1222240302): full author names Ken Peffers, Tuure Tuunanen, Marcus A. Rothenberger, Samir Chatterjee; JMIS vol 24, iss 3; published Dec 2007 (Winter 2007-8 issue). PAGE DISCREPANCY: Crossref records pp. 45-77; Peffers' own CV at kpeffers.faculty.unlv.edu and many secondary citations give pp. 45-78. Recommend citing 45-77 (Crossref/publisher) and being aware the 45-78 form is common. Also note the second author's initials are commonly mis-rendered as 'Rothenberger, A. M.' in citation databases (e.g. SCIRP); the correct form is Marcus A. Rothenberger.
sources.what_it_establishes: The DSRM process model: six activities (1) problem identification and motivation, (2) definition of objectives for a solution, (3) design and development, (4) demonstration, (5) evaluation, (6) communication - plus four possible research entry points (problem-centred, objective-centred, design/development-centred, client/context-initiated) and an explicit nominal presentation structure for DSR papers and theses.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This supplies the actual skeleton of the methodology chapter and the shape of the three-study programme. The thesis is a problem-centred initiation: VEGO-AI already produces substantial/occasional verdicts, but those verdicts are ungoverned and their uncertainty is not routed to a human. Peffers' six activities give a defensible way to present each sub-question as one DSRM iteration - SQ1 iterates on the intervention-trigger objective, SQ2 on the judgment-representation objective, SQ3 on the transfer objective - with demonstration and evaluation repeated per iteration rather than once at the end. It is also the single most-expected citation when a committee asks 'what is your research process?'

sources.authors: Shirley Gregor, Alan R. Hevner
sources.title: Positioning and Presenting Design Science Research for Maximum Impact
sources.venue: MIS Quarterly, Vol. 37, No. 2, pp. 337-355
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.25300/misq/2013/37.2.01, authors Shirley Gregor and Alan R. Hevner, MIS Quarterly vol 37 iss 2, pp 337-355, 2013. Metadata matches the requested citation exactly.
sources.what_it_establishes: The DSR knowledge contribution framework - a 2x2 of solution maturity against application-domain maturity yielding four contribution types: routine design, improvement, exaptation, and invention. Also introduces the levels of design-knowledge abstraction (Level 1 situated instantiation, Level 2 nascent design theory / operational principles, Level 3 well-developed design theory) and a publication schema for DSR.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the single most strategically important methodology citation for this thesis, because it is what turns two potential criticisms into named, respectable contribution types. SQ1 and SQ2 sit in the *improvement* quadrant: a known problem (expert effort is scarce, AI verdicts on variability are uncertain) met with a new solution (a governed selective-intervention and judgment-reuse mechanism). SQ3 - carrying the mechanism from software/UML modelling into healthcare guideline operationalization - is textbook *exaptation*, and Gregor & Hevner is the citation that makes exaptation a legitimate contribution rather than a reviewer's 'you just applied it somewhere else'. The abstraction levels also give the thesis precise language for what the judgment repository outputs: Level 2 nascent design theory, not just a Level 1 tool.

sources.authors: Salvatore T. March, Gerald F. Smith
sources.title: Design and natural science research on information technology
sources.venue: Decision Support Systems, Vol. 15, No. 4, pp. 251-266
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.1016/0167-9236(94)00041-2, authors Salvatore T. March and Gerald F. Smith, Decision Support Systems vol 15 iss 4, pp 251-266, 1995. Note the second author is Gerald F. Smith (not Smith, G. R. or similar variants that appear in some reference lists).
sources.what_it_establishes: The pre-Hevner foundation: a 2x4 research framework crossing two activities (build, evaluate - later extended to theorise and justify) with four artifact types (constructs, models, methods, instantiations). Crucially, it draws the epistemological line that design science is evaluated on *utility* while natural science is evaluated on *truth*.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The utility-versus-truth distinction is load-bearing for SQ1 in particular. Selective intervention has no ground truth to be right about: there is no gold-standard answer to 'should the system have asked a human here?' independent of what it cost the expert and what it bought the assessment. March & Smith is the citation that licenses evaluating the intervention policy on utility criteria (expert effort saved per uncertainty resolved, verdict stability, expert acceptance) rather than on classification accuracy alone - which is exactly where a purely ML-framed examiner will push back. It also supplies the artifact vocabulary that Hevner et al. 2004 inherit, so citing both shows the lineage rather than treating 2004 as year zero.

sources.authors: Roel J. Wieringa
sources.title: Design Science Methodology for Information Systems and Software Engineering
sources.venue: Springer, Berlin/Heidelberg (book); ISBN 978-3-662-43838-1 (print), 978-3-662-43839-8 (eBook)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref API (DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8): monograph, sole author Roel J. Wieringa, Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2014, ISBNs 9783662438381 / 9783662438398. Individual chapter DOIs also resolve (e.g. _1 'What Is Design Science?', _11 'Research Design'). Author affiliation University of Twente confirmed via research.utwente.nl and Wikipedia.
sources.what_it_establishes: The software-engineering-facing design science text. Introduces the engineering cycle (problem investigation, treatment design, treatment validation, treatment implementation, implementation evaluation) nested around the design cycle; the hard separation between *design problems* and *knowledge questions*; the treatment/artifact-in-context distinction; validation models and scaling-up; and Technical Action Research as a validation method.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the DSR reference that speaks the language of the thesis's actual empirical setting - UML domain models, a MODELS-published artifact, an SE audience - where the IS-flavoured Hevner/Peffers vocabulary alone can read as foreign. Three specific uses: (a) the design-problem vs knowledge-question split gives a clean way to write each sub-question twice, once as a design problem ('design a trigger policy that...') and once as a knowledge question ('to what extent does policy X reduce expert burden...'); (b) the artifact-in-context framing states precisely what SQ3 is worried about - the treatment is only ever validated in a context, so transfer claims must be argued by architectural similarity of contexts, not statistical induction; (c) Technical Action Research is a plausible design for the expert-in-the-loop studies where the researcher is also the tool-builder, which is this project's real situation.

sources.authors: Maung K. Sein, Ola Henfridsson, Sandeep Purao, Matti Rossi, Rikard Lindgren
sources.title: Action Design Research
sources.venue: MIS Quarterly, Vol. 35, No. 1, pp. 37-56
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.2307/23043488, all five authors in the stated order, MIS Quarterly vol 35 iss 1, pp 37-56, 2011. Cross-checked against AIS eLibrary record aisel.aisnet.org/misq/vol35/iss1/5/ and the MISQ publisher page. As with Hevner 2004 the indexed DOI is the JSTOR one.
sources.what_it_establishes: Action Design Research (ADR): a four-stage method - (1) problem formulation, (2) building, intervention and evaluation (BIE) as a single intertwined activity rather than build-then-evaluate, (3) reflection and learning, (4) formalization of learning - grounded in the premise that IT artifacts are *ensembles* emergent from their organizational context. Introduces 'guided emergence' and the principle of authentic and concurrent evaluation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: ADR is the closest existing methodological precedent for what SQ2 proposes to do procedurally. Stage 3 (reflection and learning) and stage 4 (formalization of learning) describe capturing what participants judged during use and converting it into reusable design knowledge - which is structurally the same move as capturing expert judgment on a variability verdict and storing it for reuse. The difference is the thesis's contribution: ADR formalizes learning *as a research output at the end*, whereas SQ2 asks how to formalize, validate and reconcile it *inside the running system*, continuously and with governance. So ADR gives both a method to borrow from and a sharp point of contrast to state the novelty. Its ensemble premise is also the strongest existing warning that an artifact shaped by one context may not transfer - i.e. the exact 'unsafe generalization' risk SQ3 names, stated by an authority the committee already respects.

sources.authors: John Venable, Jan Pries-Heje, Richard Baskerville
sources.title: FEDS: a Framework for Evaluation in Design Science Research
sources.venue: European Journal of Information Systems, Vol. 25, No. 1, pp. 77-89
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.1057/ejis.2014.36, authors John Venable, Jan Pries-Heje, Richard Baskerville, EJIS vol 25 iss 1, pp 77-89, year 2016. Note the DOI string contains '2014' because the paper was published online-first in 2014; the journal issue and the correct citation year are 2016. Some reference lists incorrectly cite it as 2014 - use 2016.
sources.what_it_establishes: The Framework for Evaluation in Design Science: two orthogonal dimensions - functional purpose (formative vs summative) and paradigm (artificial vs naturalistic) - producing four evaluation strategies: Quick & Simple, Human Risk & Effectiveness, Technical Risk & Efficacy, and Purely Technical. Also a four-step process for constructing an evaluation design (explicate goals, choose strategy, determine properties to evaluate, design the individual episodes).
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the backbone of the evaluation chapter and the direct answer to 'how will you evaluate a human-judgment governance layer?'. The dominant risk in this thesis is *human*, not technical - experts over-trusting the AI's substantial/occasional verdict, refusing to engage, being over-burdened, or having their authority quietly eroded by reuse - which places the work squarely in FEDS' Human Risk & Effectiveness strategy. That strategy prescribes early formative artificial evaluation followed by progressively more naturalistic summative evaluation, which is precisely the staged design this project needs: formative runs against the existing labelled VEGO-AI model corpus (artificial, cheap, no expert cost), then naturalistic episodes with real modelling experts, then - only if governance permits - a healthcare episode for SQ3. FEDS also gives named criteria vocabulary so the thesis can justify measuring effectiveness (real-setting) rather than only efficacy (lab).

sources.authors: Per Runeson, Martin Höst
sources.title: Guidelines for conducting and reporting case study research in software engineering
sources.venue: Empirical Software Engineering, Vol. 14, No. 2, pp. 131-164
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref API: DOI 10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8, authors Per Runeson and Martin Höst, Empirical Software Engineering vol 14 iss 2, pp 131-164. YEAR NUANCE: Crossref records the issued date as 2008 (online-first, Dec 2008); the print issue is April 2009 and the universally used citation year is 2009. dblp indexes it as journals/ese/RunesonH09 (2009). Cite as 2009. Author affiliation Lund University confirmed via portal.research.lu.se.
sources.what_it_establishes: The de facto SE-community protocol for case study research: definition of case and unit of analysis, case study design elements (objective, the case, theory, research questions, methods, selection strategy), the first/second/third-degree data collection taxonomy, triangulation types, qualitative analysis procedure, ethical considerations including informed consent, and the four validity threat categories (construct, internal, external, reliability) with a reporting checklist.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: DSR tells you to evaluate but is close to silent on how to run a rigorous empirical study with human participants; this fills that hole for the software/modelling half of the work. Three concrete uses: (a) it defines the unit of analysis question the thesis must answer explicitly - is the case a modelling cohort, a single domain model, or a single variability decision? - and getting this wrong is a standard examiner target; (b) the first/second/third-degree data taxonomy legitimises mixing system telemetry (third-degree: which verdicts triggered escalation, how long experts spent) with think-aloud or interview data (first-degree) in the same study; (c) the validity-threat taxonomy plus checklist is what the SE side of the examining panel will expect to see applied to the expert-in-the-loop studies, especially external validity, which is exactly SQ3's territory. Also gives the ethics/consent framing needed before any healthcare-adjacent work.

sources.authors: Alan R. Hevner
sources.title: A Three Cycle View of Design Science Research
sources.venue: Scandinavian Journal of Information Systems, Vol. 19, No. 2, Article 4 (pp. 87-92)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via AIS eLibrary (aisel.aisnet.org/sjis/vol19/iss2/4/): sole author Alan R. Hevner, University of South Florida; Scandinavian Journal of Information Systems vol 19 iss 2, Article 4, 2007; ISSN 1901-0990. AISeL's recommended citation gives 'Article 4' with no page range; the widely used pp. 87-92 comes from the print issue and could not be confirmed on the AISeL landing page itself. No DOI is assigned. It is a commentary on Iivari's essay.
sources.what_it_establishes: The three-cycle view: a Relevance Cycle bridging the contextual environment and the design activity (requirements in, field testing out), a Rigor Cycle bridging the knowledge base and the design activity (grounding theories and methods in, additions to the knowledge base out), and a central Design Cycle iterating build and evaluate.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: A compact, one-diagram way to show the examining committee how the whole programme hangs together, and it is more useful here than in a typical DSR thesis because this project has an unusually explicit rigor cycle. The relevance cycle is grounded in a real environment (guideline operationalization with real experts and the published VEGO-AI setting); the rigor cycle draws from two distinct knowledge bases - variability/SPL modelling on one side, human-in-the-loop uncertainty and active-learning-style deferral on the other - and the thesis's contribution flows back into both. It is also the natural place to state that VEGO-AI itself is a prior turn of the design cycle that this doctorate continues, which pre-empts 'what is yours versus what is already published?'

sources.authors: John Venable, Jan Pries-Heje, Richard Baskerville
sources.title: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluation in Design Science Research
sources.venue: DESRIST 2012, Lecture Notes in Computer Science (Design Science Research in Information Systems: Advances in Theory and Practice), Springer, pp. 423-438
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-29863-9_31, authors John Venable, Jan Pries-Heje, Richard Baskerville, Springer Berlin Heidelberg LNCS, DESRIST 2012 proceedings, pp. 423-438, 2012.
sources.what_it_establishes: The conference-paper precursor to FEDS. Sets out the ex ante / ex post and artificial / naturalistic distinctions in more detail than the journal version, plus a taxonomy of what can be evaluated and a strategy-selection procedure driven by evaluation goals and risks.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Worth citing alongside FEDS rather than instead of it, because the 2012 paper is where the ex ante versus ex post distinction is developed most usably. That distinction matters directly to SQ1: an intervention policy that is only evaluated ex post has already spent the expert time it was designed to save, so the thesis needs a defensible ex ante evaluation of candidate escalation triggers against the existing labelled corpus before any expert is put in the loop. This paper is the citation for that argument.

sources.authors: Christian Sonnenberg, Jan vom Brocke
sources.title: Evaluations in the Science of the Artificial - Reconsidering the Build-Evaluate Pattern in Design Science Research
sources.venue: DESRIST 2012, Lecture Notes in Computer Science (Design Science Research in Information Systems: Advances in Theory and Practice), Springer, pp. 381-397
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-29863-9_28, authors Christian Sonnenberg and Jan vom Brocke, Springer Berlin Heidelberg LNCS, DESRIST 2012, pp. 381-397, 2012. A companion paper by the same authors, 'Evaluation Patterns for Design Science Research Artefacts' (DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-33681-2_7, CCIS, pp. 71-83, 2012), also verified and may be cited together.
sources.what_it_establishes: The EVAL1-EVAL4 evaluation pattern: EVAL1 (ex ante, evaluating the problem/design proposal before anything is built), EVAL2 (ex ante, evaluating the design specification), EVAL3 (ex post, evaluating the instantiation in an artificial setting), EVAL4 (ex post, evaluating it in a naturalistic setting). Argues against treating evaluation as a single terminal activity.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Gives the thesis a fine-grained, numbered evaluation schedule to put in a table - which is far more convincing than a prose promise to 'evaluate the artifact'. Practically, it lets the methodology chapter state that the SQ1 trigger design gets EVAL1/EVAL2 treatment against the existing VEGO-AI corpus and design-level review, that the SQ2 judgment repository gets EVAL3 on retrospective replay of stored judgments, and that only the surviving design reaches EVAL4 with live experts. That staging is not just good practice here, it is an ethical requirement given that the scarce resource being protected (expert attention) is also the measurement instrument.

sources.authors: Richard Baskerville, Abayomi Baiyere, Shirley Gregor, Alan Hevner, Matti Rossi
sources.title: Design Science Research Contributions: Finding a Balance between Artifact and Theory
sources.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems, Vol. 19, No. 5, pp. 358-376
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query: DOI 10.17705/1jais.00495, JAIS vol 19 iss 5, pp 358-376, 2018. sources.what_it_establishes: Argues that DSR contributions span a spectrum from artifact-dominant to theory-dominant and that both ends are legitimate; provides guidance on balancing the two and on how much theorising a DSR paper is obliged to do.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Pre-empts the most predictable objection to a doctorate built on top of an existing published tool: 'this is a system, where is the theory?'. This paper is the authoritative answer that an artifact-leaning contribution is a valid DSR contribution, while also setting the bar for the theoretical residue the thesis must leave behind - which here is the set of design principles for governed judgment reuse produced by SQ2. Useful in the contribution-claims section rather than the process section.

sources.authors: David Jones, Shirley Gregor
sources.title: The Anatomy of a Design Theory
sources.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems, Vol. 8, No. 5, pp. 312-335
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via Crossref (DOI 10.17705/1jais.00129), AIS eLibrary (aisel.aisnet.org/jais/vol8/iss5/19/), Semantic Scholar, and dblp (journals/jais/JonesG07) - all four index the author order as Jones then Gregor, and AISeL's own recommended citation reads 'Jones, David and Gregor, Shirley (2007)'. IMPORTANT AUTHOR-ORDER CAVEAT: this work is very widely cited in the literature as 'Gregor & Jones (2007)', and the ANU repository copy of the manuscript is headed with Shirley Gregor's name first. The two forms refer to the same article. Recommend following AISeL/Crossref (Jones & Gregor) but expect and accept 'Gregor & Jones' in other reference lists; flag this for the supervisor since Israeli/IS-department convention may prefer the Gregor-first form.
sources.what_it_establishes: The eight structural components of an IS design theory: purpose and scope, constructs, principles of form and function, artifact mutability, testable propositions, justificatory knowledge, principles of implementation, and expository instantiation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: This is the representational schema SQ2 has been looking for. SQ2 asks how expert judgment - including the system's own core reasoning - should be represented, validated, reconciled and stored so it can be reused transparently; the eight components give a ready-made, citable structure for what a stored judgment record must carry. Two components map onto SQ2's hardest requirements almost verbatim: *justificatory knowledge* is the transparency requirement (a reused judgment must carry why it was made), and *artifact mutability* is the requirement that stored judgment be revisable without loss of human authority - the paper already treats mutability as a first-class part of design knowledge rather than an afterthought. Using this schema also lets the thesis argue its output is Level 2 nascent design theory in Gregor & Hevner's terms.

sources.authors: Shirley Gregor, Leona Chandra Kruse, Stefan Seidel
sources.title: Research Perspectives: The Anatomy of a Design Principle
sources.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems, Vol. 21, pp. 1622-1652 (issue 6)
sources.verification_note: Title, authors (Shirley Gregor / Australian National University, Leona Kruse / University of Liechtenstein, Stefan Seidel), journal (JAIS), volume 21, pages 1622-1652, year 2020 and DOI 10.17705/1jais.00649 all confirmed via Crossref bibliographic query. The ISSUE NUMBER was NOT returned by Crossref ('Not specified'); issue 6 is the commonly cited value but is unconfirmed here - verify on AIS eLibrary before the final bibliography. Second author's name appears as both 'Leona Kruse' and 'Leona Chandra Kruse' in different records.
sources.what_it_establishes: A formal schema for stating a design principle, comprising aim/implementer, user, mechanism, enactor, boundary conditions, rationale (and the accompanying distinction between action-oriented and materiality-oriented formulations). Positions design principles as the primary vehicle for transferable design knowledge.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The most operationally useful source in this batch for SQ2 and SQ3 together. SQ2 needs a concrete storage format for reusable judgment; this gives one that is already accepted in the IS community, so stored judgment records can be structured as design principles rather than as an ad hoc schema the thesis has to defend from scratch. More importantly, the schema makes *boundary conditions* a mandatory field - which is precisely the anti-unsafe-generalization device SQ3 requires. A judgment captured on UML domain models that carries explicit boundary conditions can be honestly tested for whether those conditions hold in a healthcare guideline context; one stored without them cannot. This turns 'avoid unsafe generalization' from an aspiration into a representational constraint the artifact enforces.

sources.what_it_establishes: A successor/extension to FEDS by the same author team: a more prescriptive methodology for designing a design-science evaluation, rather than a framework for classifying evaluation strategies.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Two jobs in this thesis. First, it is a current, first-tier citation showing that DSR evaluation methodology is a live research conversation and not a settled 2004-2016 canon - which defends the methodology chapter against the 'your methods literature stops a decade ago' criticism that a 2026-2029 doctorate can otherwise attract. Second, since this thesis's evaluation is genuinely non-standard (evaluating a governance layer whose output is a decision about whether to ask a human), a prescriptive evaluation-design procedure is more useful than a classificatory framework. Flagged as newly published - read it before finalising the evaluation design, as it may change how the FEDS-based staging is presented.

sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Serves two practical purposes rather than a conceptual one. It is the most efficient single citation for a short 'what is DSR' framing paragraph without re-deriving Hevner 2004, and the DSR grid is a genuinely useful one-page device for scoping each of the three sub-questions on the same axes. The accompanying cases volume is also worth mining for DSR projects with human-expert involvement, which is the exemplar type this thesis most needs and which the canonical methodology papers do not supply.

It argues FOR human supervision of LLM domain modeling but stops at 'towards' - it does not give a decision rule for when the human is invoked, nor a cost model for expert burden. Use it to show the community has named the problem and not solved it. It also usefully links two of the target researchers (Cabot, Proper) in one record.

Guidelines on scoping services when in doubt, supporting efficient dismissal and correction, and making clear why the system did what it did map one-to-one onto SQ1's request design and SQ2's requirement that human authority is retained. sources.authors: Eric Horvitz
sources.title: Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces
sources.venue: SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '99), Pittsburgh, pp. 159-166
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the ACM DL record and the Microsoft Research publication page; DOI 10.1145/302979.303030, CHI 1999, pp. 159-166, single author.
sources.what_it_establishes: Twelve principles for coupling direct manipulation with interface agents, centred on considering the uncertainty of the user's goals and the user's attention, and introducing automation only where it has genuine expected value over direct manipulation.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The theoretical origin of SQ1 and the citation that gives the sub-question intellectual legitimacy. It states the decision-theoretic form of 'when should the system act versus defer to the human' that SQ1 must instantiate for agentic variability assessment. Use it to derive the triggering criterion from first principles (expected value of asking versus deciding) rather than from an ad hoc confidence threshold - and to argue that expert burden belongs in the utility function, not as an afterthought.
sources.citation_use: Theoretical foundation of SQ1's triggering criterion.

sources.authors: Hussein Mozannar, David A. Sontag
sources.title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
sources.venue: ICML 2020 (37th International Conference on Machine Learning), PMLR vol. 119, pp. 7076-7087; preprint arXiv:2006.01862
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the dblp API: exact title, both authors, ICML 2020, PMLR v119 pp. 7076-7087, plus the arXiv preprint abs/2006.01862.
sources.what_it_establishes: Consistent surrogate loss functions for jointly learning a predictor and a deferral rule, so a system learns which instances to hand to a human expert rather than predicting on them itself.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The formal machine-learning counterpart to SQ1, and the literature the thesis must engage with to avoid the charge of reinventing learning-to-defer. It supplies both the vocabulary (deferral, expert cost, consistency) and the contrast: learning-to-defer optimises a scalar loss over i.i.d. instances with a single oracle expert, whereas SQ1 operates over structured model differences, with contested expert judgement and a governance requirement. Naming that contrast precisely is a strong contribution statement.
sources.citation_use: Formal contrast case that sharpens SQ1's novelty claim.

sources.authors: Lora Aroyo, Chris Welty
sources.title: Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation
sources.venue: AI Magazine, Vol. 36, No. 1, pp. 15-24 (AAAI)
sources.verification_note: Confirmed via the Wiley Online Library record, the AAAI OJS citation service and the VU Amsterdam research portal; DOI 10.1609/aimag.v36i1.2564, AI Magazine 36(1), 2015, pp. 15-24.
sources.what_it_establishes: Exposes seven myths arising from the assumption of a single correct annotation, and proposes 'crowd truth': human interpretation is inherently subjective, and measuring annotations across a crowd captures the range of reasonable interpretations rather than noise around one answer.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: Attacks the assumption SQ2 would otherwise smuggle in - that a captured expert judgement is a ground truth to be stored and replayed. If two experts legitimately disagree on SUBSTANTIAL versus OCCASIONAL, the store must represent the disagreement, and 'reconciliation' must be a governed, sometimes-refused operation rather than an automatic merge. This paper gives the thesis the theoretical licence and the vocabulary to build that in deliberately, and it is the strongest defence against a reviewer who asks why judgements are not simply averaged.
sources.citation_use: Theoretical basis for representing disagreement in the judgement store (SQ2); defence of non-merging reconciliation.

sources.venue: Software: Practice and Experience (Wiley)

sources.what_it_establishes: A worked case study of modelling a family of related systems using Concern-Oriented Reuse, where models are modularised into reusable concerns with features, views and inter-concern dependencies.
sources.relevance_to_this_phd: The closest structural analogue to SQ2 in the modeling literature: CORE already treats a variability decision as a first-class, deferrable, reusable unit. The doctorate's move is to make the analogous unit an expert JUDGEMENT and to add what CORE does not have - validation, reconciliation of conflicting judgements, and explicit retention of human authority. Positioning against CORE turns SQ2 from 'store judgements somewhere' into a precise architectural delta.

His ensemble-artifact premise - that an IT artifact is inseparable from the organizational context that shaped it - is the strongest existing statement of the risk SQ3 is designed to manage, and citing him makes the transfer problem a recognised methodological concern rather than a self-identified weakness.

key_researchers.name: Iris Reinhartz-Berger
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Department of Information Systems, University of Haifa, Israel
key_researchers.why_relevant: Primary supervisor and first author of the VEGO-AI base paper. Critically for this doctorate she has already moved into the human-LLM co-reasoning space herself: 'Iterative vs. Plan-Driven Approaches in Human-LLM Collaborative Modeling: An Empirical Study' (with Arava Tsoury, CAiSE 2026) is the closest existing empirical baseline to SQ1 - it studies HOW the human and the LLM interleave control during modeling, which is exactly the interaction-protocol question SQ1 must sharpen into a triggering policy. key_researchers.name: Arnon Sturm
key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva, Israel
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-supervisor and VEGO-AI co-author. (1) The human-vs-machine domain-modeling experiments with Bragilovski and Dalpiaz (RE 2024; EMSE 2026) are the methodological template for SQ1 - they establish how to measure when machine-produced models help or mislead a human, which is the dependent variable a selective-intervention policy must optimise. key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Software and Information Systems Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (PhD researcher under Arnon Sturm)

His ER 2025 explainable-AI/legal paper bridges to SQ2's representation question.

key_researchers.affiliation: University of Haifa (co-author with Reinhartz-Berger and Pnina Soffer); exact current post not confirmed

Worth contacting inside the supervisor's own group before looking outside it.

key_researchers.affiliation: Head of the Software Engineering RDI Unit, Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST); affiliate professor of computer science, University of Luxembourg; FNR PEARL Chair (BESSER project)

key_researchers.name: Lola Burgueño
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor, University of Malaga (Atenea research group / ITIS Software institute), Spain
key_researchers.why_relevant: Two distinct reasons. Substantively: co-author of 'On the Utility of Domain Modeling Assistance with Large Language Models' (ACM TOSEM 2026, the MAGDA tool and user study) - a rigorous user study of whether LLM modeling assistance actually helps, which is the evaluation design SQ1 should replicate for intervention triggering rather than for suggestion quality. Her separate line on uncertainty management in software design gives SQ1 a formal vocabulary for the 'important uncertainty' that should trigger a human request. Strategically: she is General Chair of MODELS 2026, the venue of the VEGO-AI base paper.

key_researchers.name: Houari Sahraoui
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, GEODES Software Engineering Lab, Departement d'informatique et de recherche operationnelle (DIRO), Universite de Montreal, Canada; Vice-Dean, Faculty of Arts and Sciences

Thirty years of work on automating and evaluating software development means he is the natural adversary for the thesis's evaluation claims - he is the person most likely to ask whether the governed-judgement layer actually beats a well-tuned fully automatic baseline, which is exactly the comparison SQ3 must pre-empt. Received a career recognition in computing in 2026.

key_researchers.name: Jorg Kienzle
key_researchers.affiliation: School of Computer Science, McGill University, Montreal, Canada
key_researchers.why_relevant: With Mussbacher and Alam, the originator of Concern-Oriented Reuse (CORE) and the TouchCORE tool - models modularised into reusable 'concerns' with features, views and inter-concern dependencies, plus explicit work on delaying decisions in variable concern hierarchies. That last idea is a direct structural precedent for SQ2: CORE already treats a variability decision as a first-class, deferrable, reusable artifact. The thesis's contribution is to make the analogous move for expert JUDGEMENTS about variability, with validation and reconciliation added - so CORE is both the closest structural analogue and the clearest contrast case.

key_researchers.affiliation: Department of Computing and Information Systems, Trent University, Peterborough, Canada (NOT Concordia/McGill as originally assumed - he did his PhD at McGill)

An early-career collaborator rather than an examiner.

key_researchers.name: Klaus Pohl
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Software Systems Engineering, University of Duisburg-Essen; paluno - The Ruhr Institute for Software Technology, Germany
key_researchers.why_relevant: Foundational figure in software product line engineering and variability management, and co-author of the proactive-adaptation line with Metzger. His combination of variability management with requirements engineering and proactive/adaptive systems is the intellectual pedigree the thesis's variability half sits in, and his group's 'no blind trust in AI-based decisions' framing is the governance framing SQ2 needs to position against.

key_researchers.name: Andreas Metzger
key_researchers.affiliation: Senior researcher / Dr., Software Systems Engineering, University of Duisburg-Essen and paluno - The Ruhr Institute for Software Technology, Germany
key_researchers.why_relevant: The single most mechanically useful person on this list for SQ1. 'Proactive Process Adaptation Using Deep Learning Ensembles' (CAiSE 2019, with Neubauer, Bohn and Pohl) uses per-prediction RELIABILITY ESTIMATES to decide the earliest point at which an automated adaptation is trustworthy enough to fire - structurally identical to deciding the point at which an agentic assessor should stop and ask a human. His 'A User Study on Explainable Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Systems' (ACM TAAS 19(3), 2024) then supplies the human-facing evaluation half. Together they give SQ1 a ready-made, empirically validated triggering formalism to adapt rather than invent.

key_researchers.name: Klaus Schmid
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor, Software Systems Engineering, Institute of Computer Science, University of Hildesheim, Germany (previously department head at Fraunhofer IESE)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Long-standing authority on variability modeling, product line engineering and adaptive systems, and co-author of 'Generative AI And Software Variability - A Research Vision' (VaMoS 2024). That vision paper is the field's own statement of the open agenda at the generative-AI/variability intersection - it is the document against which the thesis should position SQ2 and SQ3 to show it addresses a community-recognised gap rather than a self-declared one. He is also active in VARIABILITY 2026, a likely publication venue.

key_researchers.name: Thorsten Berger
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor and Chair of Software Engineering, Ruhr University Bochum, Germany; Guest Professor, CSE Department, Chalmers University of Technology and University of Gothenburg, Sweden
key_researchers.why_relevant: Leading empiricist on software variability in real systems (Linux kernel, Android ecosystems, automotive, robotics) and co-author of the VaMoS 2024 generative-AI-and-variability vision. His empirical stance - that real variability is messy and only partly intentional - is the external validity check on VEGO-AI's SUBSTANTIAL/OCCASIONAL distinction: if that distinction is to survive SQ3's transfer test beyond student UML models, his industrial variability corpora are where it must be shown to hold.

key_researchers.name: Sven Apel
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor and Chair of Software Engineering, Saarland University / Saarland Informatics Campus, Germany; ERC Advanced Grant holder (2022)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Combines software product lines and configurable systems with explicit attention to the human factor, including empirical and neurophysiological methods. His 2026 ICSE work 'Are Humans and LLMs Confused by the Same Code? An Empirical Study on Fixation-Related Potentials and LLM Perplexity' is directly germane to SQ1: it tests whether machine uncertainty and human difficulty coincide. If they do not, a triggering policy cannot simply use model confidence as a proxy for 'the human should look at this' - which is a substantive design constraint the thesis must address.

key_researchers.name: Saleema Amershi
key_researchers.affiliation: Partner Research Manager, Microsoft Research AI Frontiers (leads the teams behind AutoGen and Magentic-One), Redmond, USA
key_researchers.why_relevant: First author of the 18 'Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction' (CHI 2019) - the canonical design vocabulary the thesis must speak when arguing what a well-governed intervention request looks like (notably: make clear what the system can do, scope services when in doubt, support efficient correction and dismissal). Her current AutoGen/Magentic-One multi-agent work is the closest industrial analogue to VEGO-AI's four-agent architecture, so she is the reference for how human authority is (or is not) preserved inside agent teams - the core of SQ2.

key_researchers.name: Eric Horvitz
key_researchers.affiliation: Microsoft (Chief Scientific Officer); was Microsoft's chief scientist at the time of the 1999 mixed-initiative work. Current exact title not independently re-confirmed for 2026
key_researchers.why_relevant: 'Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces' (CHI 1999) is the theoretical origin of SQ1. It states, decades in advance, the exact principle the thesis operationalises for agentic assessment: consider the uncertainty of the user's goals and the expected utility of acting versus asking, and only take initiative when the expected value of automation exceeds that of leaving control with the human. Any credible SQ1 chapter has to derive its triggering criterion from, or explicitly against, this decision-theoretic framing. He is also a co-author on the CHI 2019 guidelines.

key_researchers.name: Lora Aroyo
key_researchers.affiliation: Research Scientist and team lead (Data Excellence for Evaluating Responsibly), Google DeepMind / Google Research, USA
key_researchers.why_relevant: The central figure for SQ2's hardest assumption. Her CrowdTruth work ('Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation', AI Magazine 2015) and later DICES/DIVE datasets argue that disagreement between annotators is signal, not noise, and that a single gold standard is the wrong target. Applied here: when two experts disagree about whether a difference is SUBSTANTIAL or OCCASIONAL, the judgement store must not silently resolve it. Her frameworks give the thesis a defensible way to represent and preserve legitimate disagreement instead of collapsing it - and a way to decide when reconciliation is even appropriate.

key_researchers.name: Been Kim
key_researchers.affiliation: Senior Staff Research Scientist, Google DeepMind, USA
key_researchers.why_relevant: Her TCAV (Testing with Concept Activation Vectors) line is about expressing model behaviour in terms of HUMAN-defined concepts rather than raw features, and her recent 'neologism' argument is that we need new shared vocabulary for human-machine communication. That is precisely SQ2's representation problem: SUBSTANTIAL vs OCCASIONAL variability is a human concept that must be made machine-checkable without being reduced to a surface heuristic. She is the reference for how to validate that a stored judgement concept means what the expert thought it meant - and for detecting when it silently drifts across contexts (SQ3).

key_researchers.name: Fabiano Dalpiaz
key_researchers.affiliation: Professor of Software Production, Department of Information and Computing Sciences, Utrecht University, Netherlands; PI of the Requirements Engineering lab; Editor-in-Chief of Springer's Requirements Engineering journal; Steering Committee chair of REFSQ
key_researchers.why_relevant: Already a co-author of both Sturm and Bragilovski (REFSQ 2022, RE 2024, REJ 2025, EMSE 2026), so he is effectively part of the extended supervisory network. His self-stated focus - 'the synergies of AI and humans for building trustworthy software', validated through empirical experiments with industry partners - is the closest existing statement of the thesis's umbrella question in the RE community. Practically, as EiC of the RE journal and REFSQ SC chair he is the gatekeeper of the two most natural publication outlets for SQ1 and SQ2.

key_researchers.name: Henderik A. Proper
key_researchers.affiliation: Full Professor of Enterprise and Process Engineering, Business Informatics Group, TU Wien, Austria (moved from Luxembourg in January 2023)
key_researchers.why_relevant: Co-author of 'Towards Human-in-the-Loop LLM-Enabled Domain Modeling' (ER 2025) and a long-standing authority on the foundations of domain modeling in enterprise contexts. He supplies the governance and enterprise-architecture framing SQ3 needs: the question of how a modeling judgement made in one organisational context can legitimately be carried into another is his home territory, and he is the person best placed to challenge (or endorse) the claim that guideline operationalization transfers.

key_researchers.name: Roman Lukyanenko
key_researchers.affiliation: Associate Professor of Information Systems, McIntire School of Commerce, University of Virginia, USA
key_researchers.why_relevant: Works at the intersection of conceptual modeling, information quality, crowdsourcing and machine learning, and co-authored 'Intelligent Agile: Conceptual Modeling and AI for Next-Generation Agile Software Development' (HICSS 2026) WITH Arnon Sturm - so there is an existing supervisory connection. His Conceptual Modeling for Machine Learning (CMML) line argues that domain knowledge held in conceptual models should govern how ML is fed and constrained; that is the reverse-direction argument the thesis needs for SQ2, where curated human judgement governs the agentic system rather than the other way round. His information-quality and crowdsourcing work also bears on validating stored judgements.

key_researchers.name: Veda C. Storey
key_researchers.affiliation: J. Mack Robinson College of Business, Department of Computer Information Systems, Georgia State University, USA
key_researchers.why_relevant: Senior co-author with Lukyanenko on 'Conceptual Modeling: Topics, Themes, and Technology Trends' (ACM Computing Surveys, 2023) and on the HICSS 2026 Intelligent Agile paper with Sturm. ON [28] SILVA MERCADO ET AL. - THE HEADLINE FINDING FOR THIS DOCTORATE:
This paper sits directly on SQ1 and the thesis's RQ1 novelty statement needs adjusting because of it. Verdict: BOTH a foundation and a partial competitor, not a full competitor.
- What it already answers: 'when should the system ask the human' - via a rule-based (non-LLM, therefore auditable) moderator that ranks candidate questions by their potential to clarify the most uncertain aspects of the model. The thesis can no longer claim the escalation-trigger question is untouched.
- What it does NOT answer, leaving SQ1/SQ2/SQ3 defensible: (a) no persistence - the Q&A loop is per-session and per-model, with no storage, validation, reconciliation or reuse of answers, so SQ2 is entirely untouched; (b) no cost/burden model - question selection maximises clarification value with no budget, stopping rule or measured expert effort, so the 'without unnecessary expert burden' half of SQ1 is unanswered; (c) different judgment type - their uncertainty is first-order and about model content in a greenfield drafting task, whereas VEGO-AI's is second-order and comparative (is this DIFFERENCE between two models substantial or occasional?), a normative call their formulation does not address; (d) single context, so SQ3 transfer is untouched; (e) it is a 'Towards' paper - an early proposal.
- Recommended action: reposition the SQ1 contribution as GOVERNED, PERSISTENT, COST-AWARE escalation over COMPARATIVE judgments, explicitly citing [28] as the nearest prior art that establishes the escalation loop itself. Also obtain the full text (paywalled - the method summary in this report is drawn from the publisher abstract and the ER 2025 programme, NOT from reading the paper) before finalising any novelty claim, and check for a follow-up journal version.

TWO CLAIMS THE THESIS SHOULD PREPARE TO DEFEND, surfaced by this batch:
